title: 第二章　为什么首先发生在俄国？

children: 这些贫穷的村庄，这些简陋的田野，啊，长久受苦的故乡，俄罗斯人民的土地！
These poor villages, these humble fields, O native land of long suffering, Land of the Russian people!
当今世界上有两个伟大的民族……俄国人和美国人。两者都在不为人注意中成长起来……世界几乎同时得知了他们的存在和伟大……美国人同自然设置的障碍作斗争；俄国人的对手则是人。前者与荒野和野蛮生活搏斗；后者则与全副武装的文明搏斗。因此，美国人的征服靠的是犁铧，俄国人的征服靠的是刀剑。

There are at the present two great nations in the world… the Russians and the Americans. Both have grown up unnoticed … and the world learned of their existence and their greatness at almost the same time…. The American struggles against the obstacles which nature opposes to him; the adversaries of the Russian are men. The former combats the wilderness and savage life; the latter, civilization with all its arms. The conquests of the American are therefore gained by the ploughshare; those of the Russian by the sword.
英裔美国人依靠个人利益来实现自己的目的，并让人民不受引导的力量和常识自由发挥；俄国人则把社会的一切权威集中于一人之手。前者的主要工具是自由；后者是奴役。他们的起点不同，道路也不同；然而，两者似乎都被上天的意志指定去左右半个地球的命运。

The Anglo-American relies upon personal interest to accomplish his ends, and gives free scope to the unguided strength and common sense of the people; the Russian centers all the authority of society in a single arm. The principal instrument of the former is freedom; of the latter, servitude. Their starting point is different, and their courses are not the same; yet each seems marked out by the will of Heaven to sway the destinies of half the globe.
——阿列克西·德·托克维尔，《论美国的民主》，1838年

zh: 伟大的十月社会主义革命——克里姆林宫曾一贯这样称呼它——之所以值得注意，不仅因为它是一场社会主义革命，而且因为它只能发生在俄国，而不可能在别的国家发生。因为正如列宁正确认识到的那样，沙皇帝国确实是欧洲“资本主义”秩序中最薄弱的一环。但在俄国的发展模式中，究竟是什么造成了这一宿命般的弱点？又是什么历史逻辑赋予了她那不可思议的命运，使她成为第一个从资本主义跨过世界历史门槛进入社会主义的民族？
en: The Great October Socialist Revolution, as it was once invariably called by the Kremlin, is noteworthy not just because it was socialist but also because it could have occurred in no other country but Russia. For the Empire of the Tsars was indeed the weakest link in the European “capitalist” order, as Lenin correctly perceived. But what in the pattern of Russia’s development accounts for this fateful weakness? And what is the historical logic that conferred on her the improbable destiny of becoming the first nation to cross the world-historical threshold from capitalism to socialism?

zh: 关于这一逻辑，一种广为流传的看法是，旧俄国的专制和奴役只不过以社会主义的外衣在苏维埃俄国的极权主义中重演了自身。因此，俄国的命运本质上是一成不变的，她的历史可以概括为从“白鹰到红鹰”的转变。
从历史上看，这种观点在波兰和匈牙利尤为流行，在德国左派中也是如此。原因显然且充分：从十八世纪后期起，俄国力量就经常而粗暴地干预这一地区——从1772至1796年瓜分波兰，到镇压1848年革命，再到1968年的“勃列日涅夫主义”。虽然马克思显然无法把旧俄国与其苏维埃继承者相比较，但像大多数1848年的德国人一样，他确信沙皇制度是拜占庭—蒙古式的怪物，不可能改变，也不可能最终欧洲化。
en: One widespread view of this logic is that the despotism and the servitude of old Russia simply reproduced themselves in socialist guise in the totalitarianism of Soviet Russia. Russia’s destiny, therefore, was to be essentially unchanging, and her history could be summed up as the transition from the “white to the red eagle.”

Historically, this view has been particularly prevalent in Poland and Hungary, and among Germans of the Left. This is so for the obvious and sufficient reason that from the late eighteenth century onward Russian power has regularly and brutally intervened in that area—from the Partitions of Poland between 1772 and 1796 to the crushing of the Revolution of 1848, and on down to the “Brezhnev Doctrine” of 1968. Though he obviously could not have compared old Russia with its Soviet successor, Marx, like most 1848 Germans, was convinced that tsardom was a Byzantine-Mongol monstrosity incapable of change and eventual Europeanization.

zh: 粗略一瞥历史记录，这种观点似乎有许多经验证据的支持。毕竟，旧俄国从十六世纪后期到1861年农奴解放，实行过一种近乎动产奴隶制的农奴制度，时间比欧洲任何地方都长，形式也更残酷。苏维埃俄国则通过斯大林的集体农庄制度，发展出一种新的、剥削性更强的农奴制。旧俄国把异见者和政治犯送往西伯利亚的冰原；新俄国在斯大林的古拉格中做了同样的事。最后，旧俄国一成不变的政治秩序是专制制度，其历史发展以伊凡雷帝和彼得大帝时期自上而下的专制、有时甚至疯狂的革命为标志。新的苏维埃专制则被斯大林那场更加可怕的自上而下的革命推向极致。简言之，俄国在其整个历史上一直是一种“东方专制主义”，始终与欧洲或西方截然分开、迥然不同——用黑格尔和兰克的话说，欧洲“其历史是自由的历史”。
en: On a superficial glance at the historical record, this view would seem to have much empirical evidence in its favor. Old Russia, after all, knew a regime of serfdom verging on chattel slavery from the late sixteenth century to the peasant Emancipation of 1861, that is, longer than anywhere else in Europe, and in more brutal form. Soviet Russia, in the institution of Stalin’s collective farms, developed a new and even more exploitative type of serfdom. Old Russia sent its dissidents and political prisoners to the frozen waste of Siberia; the new Russia did the same in Stalin’s Gulag. Finally, the immutable political order of old Russia was autocracy, and her historical development was marked by despotic, indeed at times insane revolutions from above under Ivan the Terrible and Peter the Great. The new Soviet autocracy was brought to its perfection by the even more terrible revolution from above of Stalin. In short, Russia throughout her history has been an “Oriental despotism” it has always been quite separate and apart from Europe or the West, “whose history is the history of freedom,” as Hegel and Ranke put the matter.

zh: 旧俄国与苏维埃俄国之间的所有这些相似之处，都有真实的事实基础。但相似并不等于连续，更不等于因果解释。因为在这幅单色图景中缺少的，是能把我们从伊凡和彼得带到列宁和斯大林的、有经验证据记载的传递者。此外，1917年的俄国人民以及外部世界，都对十月带来的激进断裂有着压倒性的印象。这应使我们怀疑，俄国历史基本连续性的论题建立在“在此之后，因而由此之故”（
）的错误原则之上。当然，这一因果原则的谬误并不意味着旧俄国没有在许多决定性方面塑造其苏维埃继承者，而只是说这一过程远比直接连续复杂得多。
en: All of these similarities between old Russia and Soviet Russia have real bases in fact. But similarities are not the same as continuities, and still less are they causal explanations. For what is lacking in this monochrome picture is the presence of empirically documented agents of transmission taking us from Ivan and Peter to Lenin and Stalin. Moreover, the Russian people in 1917, as well as the outside world, had the overwhelming impression of a radical break in October. And this should lead us to suspect that the thesis of basic continuity in Russian history is founded on the fallacious principle of

, of “after this, therefore because of this.” The fallacy of this causal principle, of course, does not mean that old Russia did not mold its Soviet successor in many decisive ways, but simply that the process through which this occurred was much more complex than one of direct continuity.

zh: 俄国与欧洲
en: RUSSIA AND EUROPE

zh: 认为俄国在其整个历史上一直是“东方专制主义”的论题，显然与另一种观念并驾齐驱：存在一个清晰而独特的对照实体，叫做“欧洲”或“西方”。换言之，在这种解释中，我们面对的是形而上学意义上的不变文化本质。事实上，现代的大多数人都不假思索地如此行事，仿佛欧亚二分法从一开始就内置在世界历史之中。暂时撇开俄国不谈，当我们说“欧洲”和“西方”时，实际上谈的是什么？
en: The thesis that Russia throughout her history has been an “Oriental despotism” obviously goes

with the idea that there exists a clear and distinct contrasting entity called “Europe” or “the West.” In other words, in this interpretation we are dealing with unchanging cultural essences in the metaphysical sense of that word. Indeed, most people in the modern age function automatically as if the Europe-Asia dichotomy was built into world history from the beginning. Leaving Russia aside for the moment, what are we in fact talking about when we speak of “Europe” and “the West”?

zh: 欧洲一词作为地理术语早在希腊人那里就出现了，最初只指爱琴海半岛。当然，它最终指整个今天称为欧洲的地区，而在1815年维也纳会议上，其东部边界被正式定在乌拉尔山。然而，用欧洲一词指称一种文化或文明，却是非常晚近的事，只能追溯到十八世纪。当时它还带有这样的含义：该地区代表人类最开明、最文明的部分，代表历史发展的顶点。
en: The word Europe as a geographical term appeared as early as the Greeks and at first referred only to the Aegean Peninsula. Eventually, of course, it came to refer to the whole of what is now called Europe, and at the Congress of Vienna in 1815 its eastern frontier was officially fixed at the Urals. The use of the term Europe to designate a culture or a civilization, however, is of very recent vintage, dating only from the eighteenth century. And at that time it also took on the connotation that the area in question represented the most enlightened and civilized portion of mankind, and the culmination of historical development.

zh: 然而，早在十八世纪之前，欧洲各民族就已清楚地意识到自己的亲缘关系和独特性，并对自身在世界上的优越地位抱有崇高看法。不过，这种独特性是用宗教而非世俗术语界定的。因此，他们把自己的社会称为基督教世界（

）——后者曾以政治而非宗教术语界定帝国，即使在君士坦丁治下基督教成为其主导宗教之后也是如此。为了强调这种价值变化，加洛林王朝开始从基督诞生之年计算年份（并标为
，即公元），而不是像此前的基督徒那样沿用希伯来方式，从世界创世之初计算。
en: Yet well before the eighteenth century, the European peoples had a clear sense of their kinship and distinctiveness, as well as an exalted view of their preeminence in the world. This distinctiveness, however, was defined in religions, not in secular terms. They thus referred to their society as Christendom (
, or the
), a term created under the Carolingian Empire, which viewed itself as the continuation of the Roman Empire reborn as a higher, Christian entity. And this new term replaced the older word

, which had defined the Empire—even after Christianity under Constantine had become its dominant religion—in political, not religious, terms. To emphasize this change in values, the Carolingians started counting the years from the birth of Christ (and numbering them
, or A.D.) rather than from the beginning of the world, which was the Hebrew manner previously used by Christians.

zh: 诚然，东方帝国也是基督教的；但在那里，希腊教会仍从属于国家，因此这些“拜占庭人”继续把自己的世界称为“罗马性”。他们也没有改变历法，以表明自己生活在一个新的弥赛亚时代；这种革命性自负，只有被拜占庭希腊人此时视为“野蛮西方”的那个西方才具有。帝国“罗马性”旧世界的这一分裂，当然就是“西方”作为一种不同于“东方”“亚洲”或“东方世界”的文明这一观念的起源。随着几个世纪过去，这个曾经落后的西方开始认为自己高于东方所有停滞的邻邦。
en: To be sure, the Eastern Empire was also Christian; but there the Greek Church remained subordinate to the state, and these “Byzantines,” therefore, continued to call their world

. Nor did they change their calendar as a sign that they lived in a new, messianic era; this revolutionary pretension was characteristic only of what the Byzantine Greeks now viewed as the “barbarian West.” This division of the old world of Imperial

is, of course, the origin of the idea of “the West” as a civilization distinct from “the East,” or “Asia,” or “the Orient.” And with the passage of centuries this once backward West would come to regard itself as higher than all its stagnant neighbors to the East.

zh: 今天所谓的欧洲，是从查理曼之后一千年间西方或拉丁基督教世界产生的文明，这个文明是在与东方基督教和伊斯兰教的对立中界定自身的。在地理上，它包括加洛林帝国的土地——法国、低地国家、意大利北部、德国西部——以及不列颠群岛。在接下来的四个世纪里，这一地区通过使西斯拉夫人和斯堪的纳维亚人皈依而向东、向北扩展；它还通过一系列十字军东征向南扩展，征服了伊比利亚半岛和意大利南部。然后，在十六世纪，这个充满活力的基督教世界以一次巨大的飞跃扩展，囊括了整个西半球；与此同时，它的航海者向东航行到印度和中国，从而第一次实现了地球的统一。因此，无论这对人类大多数多么不公平，现代世界事实上是一个欧洲中心主义的创造物。
en: What is now called Europe is the civilization that came out of Western, or Latin, Christendom during the millennium after Charlemagne, a civilization that defined itself in opposition to both Eastern Christianity and Islam. Geographically, this included the lands of the Carolingian Empire—France, the Low Countries, northern Italy, western Germany—and the British Isles. Over the next four centuries this area expanded east and north by converting the Western Slavs and the Scandinavians; it also expanded south, in a series of Crusades, by conquering the Iberian Peninsula and southern Italy. Then, in the sixteenth century, this dynamic Christendom grew in a quantum leap to take in the whole Western hemisphere; at the same time, its navigators traveled east to the Indies and Cathay, thereby for the first time achieving the unity of the planet. Thus, however unfair it may be to most of mankind, the modern world is in fact a Eurocentric creation.

zh: 换言之，欧洲或西方并不是一个固定的地理实体。它也不是一个一成不变的文化实体，因为最初的中世纪天主教文明在其扩张过程中接受了许多叠加层。只提最明显、最重要的：随着十五世纪的古典人文主义，这一文明开始世俗化；随着十六世纪新教改革的宗教分裂，拉丁基督教世界的统一被打碎。然后，如前所述，十七世纪的科学革命在十八世纪产生了启蒙运动公开反宗教的挑战。结果，基督教世界的文化在该词的两个意义上都被世俗化了：宗教被逐出生活的中心，而原先宗教性的、超越性的价值常常被转化为理性主义的、内在的价值。正是在这一转折点上，也由于这种新的世俗化文化，十八世纪的“欧洲”一词取代了“基督教世界”一词。再加上十八世纪标志着欧洲进入持续经济增长的伟大起飞，我们便得到这样一幅图景：西方是一个能动的、扩张的实体，欧洲则是一场“流动的盛宴”，新的民族不断能够加入其中。
en: In other words, Europe, or the West, is not a fixed geographical entity. Nor is it a static cultural quantity, for the initial medieval Catholic civilization received numerous overlays in the course of its expansion. To mention only the most obvious and most important: With the classical humanism of the fifteenth century, this civilization began to be secularized; and with the religious schism of the Protestant Reformation in the sixteenth century, the unity of Latin Christendom was shattered. Then, as already noted, the Scientific Revolution of the seventeenth century produced the overtly antireligious challenge of the Enlightenment in the eighteenth century. As a result, the culture of Christendom was secularized in the two meanings of that word: Religion was displaced from the center of life, and formerly religious and transcendent values were often transmuted into rationalistic and immanent ones. It is at this juncture, and because of this new secularizing culture, that in the eighteenth century the term Europe displaced the term Christendom. Add to this the fact that the eighteenth century marked the great takeoff of Europe into sustained economic growth, and we have a picture of the West as a dynamic, expanding entity, and of Europe as a “moveable feast” in which new nations were constantly able to join.

zh: 俄国当然在十八世纪初彼得大帝时期加入了这一扩张中的欧洲协调体系。然而，这一事件对双方都不是巨大的冲击，因为俄国加入的欧洲在两个方面与俄国相近。
第一，启蒙运动已削弱了东西方基督教之间对抗曾经具有的中心重要性；因此，在大多数受过教育的同时代人眼中，彼得大帝和叶卡捷琳娜大帝的“开明专制”使他们的帝国显得是欧洲的真正一部分。第二个相近之处在于，西方旧制度专制主义的社会和政治形式，与彼得之前莫斯科沙皇国可称为普遍服役国家的东西，并没有惊人差异。因此，十八世纪的新俄罗斯帝国或多或少成为一个欧洲式的旧制度，或者，如果愿意的话，一个军事君主国。
en: Russia, of course, joined this expanding Concert of Europe under Peter the Great at the beginning of the eighteenth century. This event was not a great shock to either party, however, because the Europe Russia joined was kindred in two respects.

The first was that the Enlightenment had softened the once central importance of the antagonism between Western and Eastern Christianity; consequently, the “enlightened despotism” of Peter the Great and Catherine the Great, in the eyes of most educated men of the age, made their Empire seem a genuine part of Europe. The second factor of kinship was that the social and political forms of Western old-regime absolutism were not strikingly different from what might be called the universal service state of the tsardom of Muscovy before Peter. Thus the new Imperial Russia of the eighteenth century became more or less a European-style Old Regime, or, if one prefers, a military monarchy.

zh: 因此，对于这个新的早期现代欧洲中的俄国，最好不是用“俄国与西方”的对立来理解，而是把它看作一个全大陆性东西连续体的一部分，或德国人所谓的东西文化梯度的一部分。在这种视角下，俄国是欧洲旧制度渐变序列的东端，这个序列从更精致、更发达的一端延伸到更简单、更残酷的一端。简言之，她是欧洲落后的后卫，处于东西文化梯度斜坡的底部。
en: Russia in this new, early modern Europe, therefore, is best understood not in terms of the antithesis “Russia and the West,” but as part of a continentwide West-East continuum, or of what the Germans call the West-East cultural gradient. In this perspective, Russia is the eastern extreme of a gradation of European Old Regimes running from the more elaborate and developed to the more simple and brutal. In short, she is the backward rear guard of Europe at the bottom of the slope of the West-East cultural gradient.

zh: 事实上，这种看法在莱茵河以东的民族中很常见，在德国人、波兰人、尤其是俄国人中间都是如此；这些民族各自都有越来越多的“西方”欧洲层次可供比较自身的发展，因而更清楚地意识到发展的梯度。例如，列昂·托洛茨基那曾经著名的“不平衡与综合发展规律”所表达的正是这种看法；他的意思是，俄国的落后迫使她压缩或缩短那些在更远的西方经历漫长时间和许多阶段的发展阶段。
en: This view of the matter is, indeed, a frequent perception in nations east of the Rhine, among the Germans, the Poles, and especially the Russians; each of these nations has progressively more layers of “Western” Europe to compare its own development with, and hence, is more conscious of the gradations of development. It is this perception that is expressed, for example, in Leon Trotsky’s once famous “law of combined and uneven development,” by which he meant that Russia’s backwardness forced her to compress or telescope stages of development that farther West were spread out over a long period and many stages.

zh: 这种比较文化视角最精致的表达，是亚历山大·格申克龙在《历史视角下的经济落后》中给出的。

格申克龙主要关心经济发展和工业化历史。他的论题是：在欧洲越往东，社会就越农业化、越落后，因此，为了赶上由大陆西缘不断抬高的现代性标准，它们必须移动得越快。在这种条件下，这种加速转型唯一可能的主体是国家。因此，越往东——从路易-菲利普和拿破仑三世的法国，到1830年代关税同盟的普鲁士，再到1890年代财政大臣谢尔盖·维特治下的俄国——国家在强制发展中的作用就越大。与此相应还有一个文化上的推论：从拿破仑三世时期的圣西门主义到维特时期的“合法马克思主义”，社会主义意识形态在推动这种自上而下的强制发展中发挥了越来越重要的作用。这里将遵循的正是这个“模型”。不过，它将以一种经过调整和扩展的形式使用，应用于一般的历史变迁，而不是专指经济发展。
en: The most sophisticated expression of this comparative cultural perspective is that given by Alexander Gerschenkron in his

Gerschenkron was primarily concerned with economic development and the history of industrialization. His thesis is that the farther east in Europe one goes, the more agrarian and backward societies become, and, therefore, the faster the pace at which they must move to catch up with a constantly rising standard of modernity set by the western edge of the continent. Under these circumstances the only possible agent for such accelerated transformation is the state. Thus, the farther east one goes—from the France of Louis Philippe and Napoleon III, to the Prussia of the Zollverein in the 1830s, to the Russia of Finance Minister Sergei Witte in the 1890s—the greater the role of the state in forcing development. To this there is a cultural corollary, namely, that socialist ideologies from Saint-Simonism under Napoleon III to “legal Marxism” under Witte played an increasingly important role in promoting this forced development from above. It is this “model” that will be followed here. However, it will be used in an adapted and expanded form, applied to historical change generally, rather than to economic development specifically.

zh: 现代俄国的落后不仅是经济上的；它是全方位的，同时涉及经济、社会、政治和文化。然而，在俄国历史的整个过程中，情况并非一直如此。所以，让我们从开头和基本事实开始。
en: Modern Russia’s backwardness was not just economic; it was all-encompassing, involving the economic, the social, the political, and the cultural at once. Yet this had not been the case uniformly throughout Russian history. So let us begin with the beginning and with the basics.

zh: 产生十月革命和苏维埃政权的俄罗斯帝国，脱胎于莫斯科大公国——东斯拉夫土地一角曾经很小的核心。莫斯科本身是更早实体基辅大公国、或更简单地说“罗斯”（

）的碎片。基辅罗斯有着相当典型的后罗马欧洲起源，于九世纪成形，与更西边同时代的法兰克加洛林国家同时：它是一个野蛮人王国，通过皈依罗马世界的基督教而获得合法性并晋升为文明地位；但在这里，皈依的是东部首都君士坦丁堡的基督教，而不是旧罗马的基督教。简言之，基辅罗斯像所有未来的欧洲国家一样，代表了罗马、基督教和野蛮人要素的融合，这是欧洲公式的基础——尽管就基辅而言，涉及的是另一群野蛮人以及罗马性和基督教的不同变体。换言之，基辅是欧洲基本主题的一个变奏。
en: The Russian Empire that produced the October Revolution and the Soviet regime grew out of the Grand Principality of Muscovy, a once small nucleus in a corner of the East Slavic lands. Muscovy itself was a fragment of an earlier entity, the Grand Principality of Kiev, or, more simply,
. Kievan

had a rather typical post-Roman, European origin, and it took shape, in the ninth century, at the same time as its Frankish Carolingian contemporary farther west: It was a barbarian kingdom that achieved legitimation and promotion to civilized status by conversion to the Christianity of the Roman world, but in this case it was the Christianity of the eastern capital, Constantinople, rather than that of old Rome. In short, Kievan

, like all future European states, represented a fusion of Roman, Christian, and barbarian elements that is the foundation of the European formula—though in the case of Kiev a different group of barbarians and different variants of
and Christianity were involved. In other words, Kiev was a variation on the fundamental European theme.

zh: 基辅原国家充满希望的发展，在十三世纪因君士坦丁堡的商业衰落、尤其是蒙古人对罗斯大部分地区的征服而中断。结果是东斯拉夫世界碎裂。这个世界的西部——即今天的白俄罗斯和乌克兰的很大一部分——贵族继承了权力，他们的领地最终被并入波兰—立陶宛联邦的“贵族共和国”。在北方，诺夫哥罗德共和国延续了基辅古老的商业和城市文明，但此时已转向从佛兰德斯到波罗的海的一连串汉萨城市。而在东北部，东欧平原最贫穷、最落后的部分，从罗斯的残骸中幸存下来的是王公的权力，而不是贵族或商业城市的权力。
en: The promising development of the Kievan protostate was interrupted in the thirteenth century by the commercial decline of Constantinople and especially by the Mongol conquest of most of

itself. The result was a fractured East Slavic World. The western part of this world—what is now Belarus and a good part of Ukraine—the nobility inherited power, and their territories were eventually absorbed into the “noble republic” of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth. In the north, the Republic of Novgorod continued the old commercial and municipal civilization of Kiev, but this was now oriented towards the string of Hanseatic cities from Flanders to the Baltic Sea. And in the northeast, the poorest and most backward part of the East European plain, it was the power of the prince, not that of the nobility or of the commercial municipalities, that survived from the wreckage of

zh: 正是在这个东北森林地带，到十五世纪后期，莫斯科作为一个专制强国出现，终于能够摆脱“鞑靼枷锁”。但这种新获得的自由并不意味着自动回归欧洲，因为在十五世纪初教会最终分裂之后，莫斯科对西方深怀疑惧，认为那里是一个沦于“拉丁异端”的世界。这个专制的莫斯科，因两个世纪对抗蒙古人的斗争而军事化，随后扼杀了自由的诺夫哥罗德并吞并其土地；从十七世纪开始，它着手征服波兰—立陶宛。最后，在开明的十八世纪，彼得和叶卡捷琳娜通过接管今天的波罗的海国家和波兰的大部分，完成了这一过程，从而赋予俄罗斯帝国基本的现代形态。为了圣化这一结果，并宣示与最骄傲的欧洲列强平起平坐，彼得采用了旧东罗马的皇帝头衔，从而为莫斯科国家声称拥有欧洲历史传统中的至高尊严。
en: It was in this northeastern forest zone, by the late fifteenth century, that Muscovy emerged as an autocratic power capable at last of freeing itself from the “Tatar yoke.” But this new freedom did not mean an automatic return to Europe, for Muscovy, after the final schism of the Churches in the early fifteenth century, regarded the West with deep suspicion as a world given over to the “Latin heresy.” This autocratic Muscovy, militarized by its two-century struggle against the Mongols, then snuffed out free Novgorod and annexed its lands; beginning in the seventeenth century, it started on the conquest of Poland-Lithuania. Finally, in the enlightened eighteenth century, Peter and Catherine completed this process by taking over the present-day Baltic states and the lion’s share of Poland, thus giving the Russian Empire its basic modern form. To consecrate this result, and to assert equality with the proudest European powers, Peter took the Imperial title of old East Rome, thereby claiming for the Muscovite state the supreme dignity in the European historical tradition.

zh: 因此，现代俄罗斯帝国是由东斯拉夫土地中最落后、最原始、最军事化的部分创造的；这一地区之所以产生这种征服力量，恰恰因为它是抵御草原野蛮人的边防地区。在这方面，俄国的经验与现代德国的经验相似：正是落后、军事化、专制的勃兰登堡—普鲁士，最终吸收了德语地区更发达的西部和南部。
en: Thus the modern Russian Empire was created by the most backward, primitive, and militarized portion of the East Slavic lands, an area that generated this conquering power precisely because it was a frontier march against the steppe barbarians. In this respect the Russian experience is similar to the modern German one, in which it was a backward, militarized, and autocratic Brandenburg-Prussia that wound up absorbing the more developed western and southern portions of the German-speaking lands.

zh: 落后在俄国帝国建国中产生政治优势的动力，必须从彼得之前莫斯科的内部发展中寻找。
莫斯科位于北欧森林平原的东北端，土壤比欧洲其他地方更贫瘠，气候更严酷，生长季节更短。只提最基本的事实：十二世纪发生在远西欧洲、十四世纪到达中欧的三圃制农业革命，直到十五世纪下半叶才来到莫斯科；商业城镇只能追溯到十六世纪，直到十九世纪才成为显著因素。这一切的结果是，莫斯科国家（以及后来的俄罗斯帝国）的物质基础极其薄弱。
en: The dynamic of the political advantages of backwardness for Russian Imperial state-building must be sought in the internal development of Muscovy before Peter.

Situated at the northeastern extremity of the northern European forested plain, Muscovy had poorer soil, a harsher climate, and a shorter growing season than elsewhere in Europe. To mention only what is most basic: The agricultural revolution of the three-field system that occurred in far-western Europe in the twelfth century, and that reached central Europe in the fourteenth century, did not come to Muscovy until the second half of the fifteenth century; and commercial towns date only from the sixteenth century and did not become a notable factor until the nineteenth. The result of all this was that the material base of the Muscovite state (and later that of Imperial Russia) was extremely weak.

zh: 与此同时，这个国家面临着特殊的军事问题；它暴露在南方广阔草原上游牧民族的入侵之下，而且它的任何边界都缺乏天然疆界。这就是莫斯科国家、因而也是其社会异常军事化的起源。到十六世纪，服役贵族（
）完全从属于专制的沙皇，农民被农奴化以供养贵族，而农民和人数很少的市民阶层向国家纳税，教士则为整体的成功祈祷。因此，在俄国，传统欧洲的领主—农民秩序被组织起来，以满足君主制的军事需要，这种体制最好被描述为一个普遍服役国家。
en: At the same time, this state confronted exceptional military problems; It was exposed to nomadic incursions from the vast open steppes to the south, and it lacked natural frontiers at any of its borders. This was the origin of the exceptional militarization of the Muscovite state and, therefore, of its society. By the sixteenth century, the service gentry, or

, was wholly subordinated to the autocratic tsar, and the peasants were enserfed to support the gentry, while both the peasants and the small class of townsmen paid taxes to the state, and the clergy prayed for the success of the whole. Thus, in Russia the lord-peasant order of traditional Europe was organized to meet the military needs of the monarchy in what is best described as a universal service state.

zh: 彼得大帝所做的，是按照旧制度欧洲其他地区军事专制主义的模式，或多或少地改造这套原始安排。

所有这些早期现代国家形成的关键，是需要投入一支庞大的常备军。直到十七世纪初，欧洲的军事力量由后封建民兵、贵族征召兵或雇佣军组成。由于多种无需在此赘述的原因，直到十七世纪中叶，一支正规而永久的常备军——人人都穿国王的制服，最终驻扎在他的兵营里——才成为任何希望在国际上保持竞争力的国家的必需。当然，这一发展的伟大典范是路易十四的法国，但古斯塔夫·阿道夫的瑞典和大选帝侯的勃兰登堡—普鲁士同样是恰当的例子。在每一种情况下，国家的内部行政和财政制度都必须调整以满足这些军事需要。在这样一个世界里，未能及时调整结构的国家——尤其是波兰—立陶宛联邦——注定从欧洲地图上消失。
en: What Peter the Great did was to remold this primitive set of arrangements more or less on the pattern of the military absolutisms of the rest of old-regime Europe.

The key to all of these early modern state formations was the need to field a large standing army. Until the early seventeenth century, the military forces of Europe had been composed of postfeudal militias, noble levies, or mercenary units. For a variety of reasons that need not concern us here, it was only in the mid-seventeenth century that a regular and permanent standing army—one in which everyone wore the king’s uniform and that eventually would be quartered in his barracks—became a necessity for any state wishing to remain competitive internationally. The great model for this development, of course, is the France of Louis XIV, but the Sweden of Gustavus Adolphus, and the Brandenburg-Prussia of the Great Elector are equally apposite examples. In each case the internal administrative and fiscal systems of the state had to be adjusted to meet these military needs. In such a world, states that could not adapt their structures in time—notably, the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth—were fated to disappear from the map of Europe.

zh: 彼得统治下的俄国做出了异常成功的适应。路易十四可以凭借法国巨大的财富，投入四十万人对抗英国、荷兰和奥地利的联合资源。彼得凭借俄国远为微薄的资源，可以投入二十万人，这足以对付当时正在衰落的瑞典，而且两倍于当时普鲁士所能夸耀的兵力。
en: Russia under Peter made an exceptionally successful adaptation. Louis XIV, with the great wealth of France to draw on, could field four hundred thousand men against the combined resources of Britain, Holland, and Austria. Peter, with the far more meager resources of Russia, could field two hundred thousand, which was quite enough against then-declining Sweden, and twice as much as Prussia could boast at the time.

zh: 彼得通过自上而下的革命性国家行动实现了这一相当可观的功业。彼得改革的关键在于，落后的莫斯科一旦摆脱蒙古人，就面对早期现代欧洲军事革命这一远为严峻的挑战。由于俄国经济和社会过于薄弱，无法自行应对这一挑战，国家只能通过自上而下的残酷行动，动员并榨取国家的微薄资源，直到极限。这与大选帝侯五十年前以普鲁士同样微薄的资源所做之事相似。在两种情况下，由此获得的大国地位都将维持到二十世纪的灾难性战争。
en: Peter achieved this very considerable feat by revolutionary state action from above. The crux of the Petrine reform is that backward Muscovy, once freed of the Mongols, was confronted by the far more serious challenge of the early modern European military revolution. Since the Russian economy and society were too weak to meet this challenge on their own initiative, the meager resources of the country had to be mobilized and squeezed to the limit by brutal state action from above. This is similar to what the Great Elector had done fifty years earlier with the comparably meager resources of Prussia. And in both cases the great-power status that resulted would be maintained until the catastrophic wars of the twentieth century.

zh: 缩小差距
en: NARROWING THE GAP

zh: 自上而下的革命，作为落后俄国对西方挑战的回应，这一模式将一直维持到1917年旧制度的终结。

这一挑战在某种程度上始终是军事性的，因为现代战争越来越依赖先进技术。但随着时间的推移，挑战从相对简单的军事问题，演变为越来越复杂的经济、政治和文化问题。随着西方不断提高“欧洲”和“现代”的门槛，俄国不得不针对每一个新的西方发展水平，发展出相应更复杂的适应方式；而随着时间推移，通过自上而下的残酷国家行动来实现这些适应变得越来越困难。社会资源越来越需要由社会本身来动员，而社会最终从国家手中接过了现代化的任务。
en: The pattern of revolution from above as the response of backward Russia to the challenge of the West would be maintained down to the end of the Old Regime in 1917.

This challenge would always remain to some degree military, insofar as modern warfare became increasingly dependent on advanced technology. But over time the challenge would evolve from a relatively simple military matter to ever more complex economic, political, and cultural ones. As the West constantly upped the ante of what it meant to be European and modern, so Russia had to develop correspondingly more complex adaptations to each new Western level of development; and as time went by, it became increasingly difficult to make these adaptations by brutal state initiative from above. More and more, the resources of society had to be mobilized by society itself, which eventually took over the task of modernization from the state.

zh: 这些新式挑战中的第一个，是法国大革命带来的民主冲击。因为一旦专制国家在西方大部分地区不再是进步的主要力量，一旦现代性的火炬被传递给人民，俄国的专制国家也就自动过时、落后，甚至反动——首先在西方眼中如此，最终在其受教育程度日益提高的精英眼中也是如此。因此，由于俄国在新的民主观念盛行的欧洲之中仍然是一个以农奴制为基础的社会，整个制度越来越处于危险的压力之下。
en: The first of these new-type challenges was the democratic shock of the French Revolution. For once the absolutist state was no longer the major force for progress in most of the West, and when the torch of modernity had been passed to the people, the Russian autocratic state was also automatically out of date, laggard, and even reactionary, first in the eyes of the West, and ultimately in the eyes of its increasingly more educated elite. Thus, since Russia remained a serf-based society in the midst of the new Europe of the democratic idea, the whole system was increasingly placed under dangerous strains.

zh: 这些压力之所以更大，是因为彼得拼凑起来的俄国旧制度非常简陋。俄国最伟大的历史学家瓦西里·克柳切夫斯基准确地强调了俄国历史进程的极端简单性（与更西欧的国家相比），这一事实很大程度上源于其阶级结构的鲜明对立。
直到十九世纪的相当长一段时间，俄国实际上只有两个阶级，或至少只有两个重要阶级。一个是服役贵族（
），约占总人口的2%；另一个是农民，直到1890年代约占人口的95%。贵族拥有大部分财富，垄断一切特权，充任国家官僚，担任军官，此外还支配文化。农民——其中一半被农奴化于贵族，另一半属于国家——劳作以物质上维持国家，缴纳税款，并提供军队的步兵。诚然，还存在其他等级——商人和教士——但他们在人数上微不足道，在社会上的分量更小。
en: These strains were all the greater because the Russian Old Regime, as put together by Peter, was a very rudimentary affair. The greatest of Russian historians, Vasilii Kliuchevskii, has accurately emphasized the extreme simplicity of Russia’s historical processes (as compared with those of more Western European countries), a fact that derives largely from the starkness of her class structure.
Until well into the nineteenth century there were, in effect, only two classes in Russia, or at least only two that mattered. There was the service gentry (

), which constituted about 2 percent of the population; and there was the peasantry, which until the 1890s constituted roughly 95 percent of the population. The gentry possessed most of the wealth, monopolized all privileges, staffed the state bureaucracy, officered the military forces, and in addition dominated culture. The peasantry, one half of their numbers enserfed to the gentry and the other half to the state, labored to maintain the nation materially, paid taxes, and furnished the foot soldiers of the military. To be sure, other estates existed as well—the merchants and the clergy—but they were insignificant numerically and counted for even less socially.

zh: 把法国革命后的民主概念引入这样一个世界，只能产生毁灭性的效果。这种新的、激进的欧洲化形式得以发挥作用，凭借的是一个到十九世纪中叶被称为知识分子的群体。
en: The introduction of the post-French Revolutionary concept of democracy into such a world could only have a devastating effect. The means through which this new and radical form of Europeanization made itself felt was a group that came to be known by the mid-nineteenth century as the intelligentsia.

zh: 从彼得时代起，俄国国家使社会现代化的主要方式之一就是建立教育体系。这个体系从精英大学开始，后来才扩展到中学文科学校，最后到小学，力图吸收和传播西方的先进文化。最初，这是为了加强国家权力，事实上也确实起到了这种作用。但在十九世纪初，这个人数极少、绝大多数出身贵族的受教育精英，开始要求当代西方自由主义所提出的政治参与权和个人自由；这使忧心忡忡的专制政权惊慌失措，因为它始终铭记俄国长期的农民起义历史。其中最大的一次就是近在1774年的普加乔夫起义，普希金所说的“俄国式暴动（
），没有头脑，也没有怜悯”，指的正是它。
事实上，在本世纪初，极端保守的约瑟夫·德·迈斯特曾警告继续奉行自上而下启蒙传统的亚历山大一世：对帝国脆弱结构的真正危险，与其说是农民本身，不如说是有朝一日出现一个“大学里的普加乔夫”（
en: From the time of Peter, one of the principal ways in which the Russian state modernized its society was to build an educational system. Beginning with elite universities, and only later going on to secondary gymnasia and finally to elementary schools, this system sought to absorb and transmit the advanced culture of the West. Initially this was intended, and did in fact serve, to strengthen the power of the state. But in the early nineteenth century the tiny educated elite, overwhelmingly from the gentry, began to demand the rights of political participation and personal liberty put forward by contemporary Western liberalism; this only panicked the apprehensive autocracy, which was ever mindful of Russia’s long history of peasant revolts. The greatest of these, that of Pugachev as recently as 1774, was what Pushkin had in mind when he spoke of “the Russian
[anarchic riot], mindless and pitiless.”

Indeed, at the very beginning of the century, the ultraconservative Joseph de Maistre had warned Alexander I, who continued the Imperial tradition of enlightenment from above, that the real danger to the fragile structures of the Empire was not so much the peasants themselves as an eventual “

zh: 第一批这样的知识分子反叛者，在1825年亚历山大去世时穿着帝国近卫军的制服出现。这些后来被称为十二月党人的人，试图对他的继承人发动武装政变，目的是给俄国一部宪法并废除农奴制。失败后，新沙皇尼古拉一世在其三十年的统治中镇压了一切初生自由主义的表现。作为回应，贵族知识分子只是变得更加政治化，但是在理论而非实践领域。一方面，西方派论证说，尽管有尼古拉，俄国最终注定要重走欧洲通往宪政自由的道路，他们的榜样是七月王朝的法国。另一方面，斯拉夫派像德国浪漫保守派一样，害怕西方那条破坏性的道路，因此坚持俄国的发展必须建立在本土传统的家长制和村社方式之上。斯拉夫派的恐惧是有道理的，因为最激进的西方派米哈伊尔·巴枯宁和亚历山大·赫尔岑，到1848年革命时已在要求民主事务中的终极目标：社会主义。
en: The first such intellectual rebels appeared in the uniforms of the Imperial guards at Alexander’s death in 1825. These Decembrists, as they came to be called, attempted an armed coup against his heir with the aim of giving Russia a constitution and abolishing serfdom. After their failure, the new emperor, Nicholas I, repressed all manifestations of nascent liberalism throughout his thirty-year reign. In response, the gentry intellectuals only became more political, but in the theoretical, not the practical, domain. On the one hand, the Westernizers argued that Russia, despite Nicholas, was destined eventually to retrace Europe’s path to constitutional liberty, and their model was July Monarchy France. On the other hand, the Slavophiles, like the German romantic conservatives, were fearful of the disruptive Western path, and so insisted that Russia’s development must be founded on the patriarchal and communal ways of the native tradition. And well might the Slavophiles have been afraid, for the most radical Westernizers, Mikhail Bakunin and Aleksandr Herzen, by the Revolution of 1848 were demanding the ultimate in matters democratic: socialism.

zh: 然而，在俄国条件下，这种新学说不可能以无产阶级作为其普遍阶级；只有农民——人民，或“
”——才能扮演这个角色。
因此，赫尔岑和巴枯宁提出了一种新版本的社会主义乌托邦：农民社会主义，建立在村社（
）之上。这一理论后来被称为民粹主义（
），它断言农民天生就是社会主义者，因为他们没有私有财产：他们集体占有土地，并随着家庭规模的变化在村社内部定期重新分配土地。民粹主义还断言，农民天生就是革命者，因为他们是贵族领主的动产农奴。因此，俄国的民主革命将简单至极：一场农民起义将摧毁专制制度和贵族，而社会主义实际上就会以村社的形式存在。
en: Under Russian conditions, however, this new doctrine could not have the proletariat as its universal class; only the peasantry—the people, or the
—could play that role.
So Herzen and Bakunin advanced a new version of the socialist utopia: peasant socialism, founded on the village commune, or
. This theory, later known as

, or Populism, asserted that the peasants were innately socialist because they had no private property: They held their lands collectively and redistributed them periodically within the commune as families changed in size, Populism asserted further that the peasants were innately revolutionary because they were chattel serfs of their gentry lords. Consequently, the democratic revolution in Russia would be simplicity itself: A peasant uprising would destroy the autocracy and the gentry, and socialism would virtually exist in the form of the village commune.

zh: 因此，落后的俄国可以在一次革命中从旧制度直接跃入社会主义，避开西方资产阶级宪政主义的中间站。于是，正当马克思为工业西方创造出那个时代最伟大的社会幻想时，俄国也为农业东方创造了一个与之呼应、尽管更为原始的幻想：落后从负担变成了优势，欧洲最后一个民族开始把自己视为潜在的第一个民族。
en: Thus backward Russia, in a single revolution, would be able to leap directly from the Old Regime to socialism and avoid the Western halfway house of bourgeois constitutionalism. And so, at the same time that Marx created the greatest social fantasy of the age for the industrial West, Russia produced an answering, though more primitive, fantasy for the rural East: Backwardness was transformed from a burden into an advantage, and the last nation of Europe came to see itself as potentially the first.

zh: 在下一个统治时期，知识分子的激进翼获得了把民粹主义幻想付诸行动的机会。1860年代，亚历山大二世通过1861年农奴解放、随后1864年建立民选地方自治机构（

）和独立司法，进行了一场自上而下的自由化革命。这些“大改革”与1806—1810年的普鲁士改革非常相似，后者引入了法国革命议程中与保存贵族制和绝对君主制相容的那一部分。亚历山大旨在实现类似的受控现代化，而且他确实比彼得以来任何一位君主都更多地缩小了与欧洲其余部分的差距。但正如托克维尔的名言所说，坏政府最危险的时刻，正是它开始自我改革之时。果然，知识分子中较不耐烦的成员被大改革激进化，以至于产生了一场持续的革命运动。
en: In the next reign, the radical wing of the intelligentsia got its chance to act on the Populist fantasy. In the 1860s, Alexander II carried out a liberalizing revolution from above with the Emancipation of the serfs in 1861, followed by the creation of elected organs of local self-government, the

, and an independent judiciary in 1864. These Great Reforms were a close analogue of the Prussian Reform of 1806-1810, which introduced that part of the French Revolution’s agenda that was compatible with the preservation of aristocracy and absolute monarchy. Alexander’s aim was a similar controlled modernization, and he indeed narrowed the gap with the rest of Europe more than did any sovereign since Peter. But as Tocqueville famously observed, the most dangerous time for a bad government is when it starts to reform itself. And indeed, the more impatient members of the intelligentsia were radicalized by the Great Reforms to the point where they produced a continuing revolutionary movement.

zh: 这一变化在六十年代由平民“儿子”对贵族“父亲”的反叛实现——借用伊凡·屠格涅夫著名的二分法。父辈在政治上是自由派，在文化上是哲学唯心主义者和浪漫主义者；或者，当他们像赫尔岑和巴枯宁那样是社会主义者时，他们试图把德国哲学与法国社会主义、黑格尔与圣西门或蒲鲁东融合起来。那些粗鲁的儿子——常常出身教士家庭——则在他们的民粹主义之上附加了一种哲学“虚无主义”，那是实证主义、唯物论和功利主义伦理的咄咄逼人的混合物；在这种视角下，贵族自由派被判定为比专制制度本身更坏的进步之敌。赫尔岑把这些平民称为“胆汁质的人”，他们确实代表了欧洲启蒙传统中一个特别坚硬而粗粝的支脉。
en: This change was effected in the sixties by the revolt of the plebian “sons” against their gentry “fathers,” in Ivan Turgenev’s famous dichotomy. The latter were liberals in politics and philosophical idealists and romantics in culture; or when they were socialists, like Herzen and Bakunin, they sought to fuse German philosophy with French socialism, Hegel with Saint-Simon or Proudhon. The uncouth sons, often from clerical families, adjoined to their Populism a philosophical “nihilism” that was an aggressive compound of positivism, materialism, and utilitarian ethics; in this perspective, gentry liberals were judged to be worse enemies of progress than the autocracy itself. Herzen called these commoners “the bilious ones,” and they indeed represented a particularly hard-bitten and crude strain of the European Enlightenment tradition.

zh: 他们的伟大人物是尼古拉·车尔尼雪夫斯基，文学批评家和社会哲学家。在他的世界观中，生活的一切都从属于政治和为人民的服务。一切艺术都必须服务于公共生活，一切个人关系都必须为公共事业牺牲，一切精力都必须献给革命，而革命将把俄国带入理性社会的水晶宫。他在1863年的一部乌托邦小说《怎么办？》中阐述了这种精神；在接下来的半个世纪里，这部小说将成为越来越多投身人民事业的“忏悔的贵族”的革命祈祷书。
en: Their great figure was Nikolai Chernyshevskii, literary critic and social philosopher. In his worldview everything in life was subordinated to politics and the service of the people. All art had to be civic, all personal relationships had to be sacrificed to the public cause, and all energies devoted to the revolution which would bring Russia to the Crystal Palace of a rational society. He expounded this ethos in 1863 in a utopian novel,
, which for the next half-century would be the revolutionary breviary of the “repentant noblemen” who increasingly rallied to the people’s cause.

zh: 同一时期，这一事业变成了一场积极的革命运动。农奴解放使民粹主义者激进化，因为他们认为给农民的土地安排过于吝啬，简直是让贵族获利的“骗局”。显然，农民现在会起来进行社会主义革命。为了推进这场起义，1861年一群学生组织了一个业余密谋团体“土地与自由”。他们很快被捕，连同他们的导师、被指为同谋的车尔尼雪夫斯基；后者在流放中度过余生，这一殉道更加强化了他小说的信息。但当后来一群激进学生终于在1874年发起“到人民中去”的十字军、号召起义时，农民完全没有响应。于是，1878年后，激进分子——此时组成秘密组织“民意党”——转向针对政府的恐怖主义，希望这种震撼最终能点燃民众的爆炸。他们甚至判处沙皇死刑，并于1881年成功“处决”了他。这场对法国革命的幻想式重演，是现代世界把政治恐怖主义（区别于孤立的暗杀行为）作为系统策略的开端。因此，民粹主义自下而上群众起义的战略，与精英自上而下恐怖的战略，在俄国结合起来，在1789至1871年西方革命传统所提供的原初合法性之外，进一步赋予了政治暴力以合法性。
en: In the same years, this cause became an active revolutionary movement. The Emancipation radicalized the Populists because of what they believed was a niggardly settlement of land for the peasants, indeed a veritable “swindle” to the profit of the gentry. Clearly, the peasants would now rise up in a socialist revolution. To further this revolt, in 1861 a group of students formed an amateur conspiracy, “Land and Freedom.” They were soon arrested, along with their mentor and alleged co-conspirator, Chernyshevskii, who would spend the rest of his days in exile, a martyrdom which reinforced the message of his novel. But when a later group of radical students finally went on a “crusade to the people” in 1874 with an appeal to insurrection, the peasants totally failed to respond. So after 1878 the radicals, now grouped in the clandestine organization the “Will of the People,” turned to terrorism against the government in the hope that the shock would at last ignite the popular explosion. They even condemned the emperor to death and succeeded in “executing” him in 1881. This fantasy reenactment of the French Revolution was the beginning of political terrorism (as opposed to isolated acts of assassination) as a systematic tactic in the modern world. Thus, the Populist strategy of mass insurrection from below, in conjunction with that of elite terror from above, combined in Russia to lend further legitimacy to political violence over and above the initial legitimation provided by the Western revolutionary tradition from 1789 to 1871.

zh: 陀思妥耶夫斯基把这些新激进分子称为“群魔”，而他在1860年代和1870年代所有伟大的虚构肖像——从拉斯柯尔尼科夫到斯塔夫罗金到伊凡·卡拉马佐夫——事实上都是对俄国“虚无主义”革命知识分子所患病症的个案研究。在西方，陀思妥耶夫斯基常常主要被当作病态和神经症的心理学家，或尼采和弗洛伊德的先驱来阅读；当然，他两者都是。然而，他之所以获得这些洞见，是因为他首先是现代性的批评者，是启蒙运动以来整个欧洲文化的批评者。他发展这一批判，是为了捍卫他所认为的长期受苦的俄国人民那种谦卑而神圣的价值，而这些价值正受到当时通过大改革的缺口涌入俄国的西方现代世界的威胁。最初使他警觉这一威胁的，正是车尔尼雪夫斯基的《怎么办？》；陀思妥耶夫斯基1864年的《地下室手记》——他在其中发现了自己作为作家的真正使命——就是对车尔尼雪夫斯基那部幻想小说的直接回答。随着陀思妥耶夫斯基在民意党的恐怖运动中坚持攻击，他的反愿景变得越来越清晰：那些自称为人民之友的人，即激进知识分子，实际上是人民潜在的奴隶主——正如宗教大审判官的传说所示。
en: Dostoevsky called these new radicals “the possessed,” and all of his great fictional portraits of the 1860s and 1870s, from Raskolnikov to Stavrogin to Ivan Karamazov, are in fact case studies of the sickness inhabiting Russia’s “nihilist,” revolutionary intelligentsia. Too often, Dostoevsky has been read in the West primarily as a psychologist of morbidity and neurosis, or as a precursor of Nietzsche and Freud, and he is, of course, both of these things. Yet he came by these insights because he was in the first instance a critic of modernity, of the whole of European culture since the Enlightenment. He developed this critique to defend what he saw as the humble but holy values of the long-suffering Russian people, values menaced by the modern world of the West then bursting into Russia through the breach of the Great Reforms. And what first alerted him to this menace was Chernyshevskii’s
; Dostoevsky’s

of 1864, the work in which he discovered his true vocation as a writer, was a direct answer to Chernyshevskii’s visionary novel. And as Dostoevsky persevered in his attack down through the terror campaign of the Will of the People, his counter-vision became ever more clear: The self-proclaimed friends of the people, the radical intelligentsia, were in fact their potential slave-masters—as in the legend of the Grand Inquisitor.

zh: 因此，陀思妥耶夫斯基的主人公是对启蒙阴暗面、对理性主义潜在魔性、对高尚意图之精神病理学的研究。他的虚构探索的要旨，带有某种埃斯库罗斯式的意味：现代理性的傲慢导致道德疾病和谋杀罪行。于是，理性的父辈生出了狂热的子辈，而子辈又产生了犯罪的恐怖分子谢尔盖·涅恰耶夫。这幅阴郁的图景无疑是一种漫画，事实上对俄国自由派和西方都有些不公。但这是一个二十世纪将在很大程度上予以证实的图景，尤其是当车尔尼雪夫斯基——到1937年叶若夫恐怖时，甚至包括涅恰耶夫——的继承者掌权之后。
en: Dostoevsky’s heroes thus are studies of the dark side of enlightenment, of the potential demonism of rationalism, and of the psychopathology of noble intentions. And the burden of his fictional explorations is the somewhat Aeschylean one that the hubris of modern reason leads to moral sickness and murderous crime. Thus, the reasonable fathers begat the fanatical sons who produced the criminal terrorist Sergei Nechaev. This somber vision is a caricature no doubt, and indeed something of a libel on both the Russian liberals and the West. Yet it is a vision that the twentieth century would do much to validate, particularly once the heirs of Chernyshevskii—and by the time of the Yezhov Terror of 1937, even of Nechaev—had come to power.

zh: 陀思妥耶夫斯基的肖像也是对俄国文化特殊脆弱性的一种评论，这种脆弱性使俄国如此容易受到来自西方的一切意识形态之风的影响——正是这种局面使车尔尼雪夫斯基能够把约翰·斯图亚特·密尔清醒的功利主义和政治经济学，变成《怎么办？》中所阐述的革命精神的前提。在这种环境下，可怜的屠格涅夫——俄国理性精神在文明上的化身，其谱系从普希金延伸到契诃夫——注定成为失败者，徒劳地以自由派父辈的名义向他们的革命子辈劝诫。
en: Dostoevsky’s portraits are also a commentary on the special fragilities of Russia’s culture that made her so vulnerable to all ideological winds from the West—a situation that allowed Chernyshevskii to turn the sober utilitarianism and political economy of John Stuart Mill into the premises of the revolutionary ethos expounded in

Under such circumstances, poor Turgenev, the civilized incarnation of Russian reasonableness—in a lineage running from Pushkin to Chekhov—was condemned to run as a loser, vainly expostulating, in the name of the liberal fathers, with their revolutionary sons.

zh: 把整个事情归结为一个命题：旧制度俄国政治的巨大脆弱性在于，社会主义几乎与自由主义同时产生，这与远西欧洲的模式大不相同——在后者，经过几十年，政治赌注才被如此戏剧性地抬高。而这一切发生时，俄国的真正问题并不是社会理性的水晶宫，而是废除农奴制，如果可能的话，对专制权力施加一些有限的约束。结果是，亚历山大二世的大改革没有开启向现代政治制度的有序过渡（这一过程即使在西方也很少有序），反而开启了一场在旧制度余下岁月中不会消退的革命运动。
en: To put the whole matter in a single proposition: The great fragility of old-regime Russian politics is that socialism came into existence almost simultaneously with liberalism, a pattern quite unlike that of far—Western Europe, where several decades elapsed before the political stakes were raised so dramatically. And this occurred when the real issue in Russia was not a Crystal Palace of social reason, but the abolition of serfdom and, if possible, the achievement of some modest limitations on the power of the autocracy. The result was that the Great Reforms of Alexander II, instead of initiating an orderly transition to a modern political system (a process that was rarely orderly even in the West), inaugurated a revolutionary movement that would not abate during the remainder of the Old Regime.

zh: 欧洲没有其他国家有这样一场持续的革命运动。与英国形成极端对比：即使有悠久的议会传统，英国从1832年到1912年才完成从旧制度阶级选举权到男性普选的过渡，而直到这一时期末，社会主义才成为一支政治力量。然而，俄国在还没有任何选举权之前几十年，就已有了一个付诸枪击的社会主义运动。因此，俄国落后所产生的政治公式是：现代民主运动各阶段的压缩或缩短——以及由此而来的长期激进化。这个公式反过来产生了一种对革命的真正崇拜，把革命视为现代政治过程的最高形式。
en: And no other country in Europe had such a continuing revolutionary movement. To make the extreme contrast with Britain: It took Britain, even with a long prior parliamentary tradition, from 1832 to 1912 to effect the transition from an old-regime class suffrage to universal manhood suffrage, and only at the end of this period did socialism become a political force. Russia, however, had a shooting socialist movement decades before she had any suffrage at all. The political formula produced by Russian backwardness, then, is the compression or telescoping—and thus the chronic radicalization-of the stages of the modern movement towards democracy. This formula, in turn, produced a veritable cult of Revolution as the highest form of the modern political process.

zh: 欧洲其余部分向俄国提出的最后一项挑战，是工业革命。纺织业在1840年代到来，铁路热潮在1860年代到来，但只有通过财政大臣谢尔盖·维特在1890年代的努力，才谈得上俄国发生了革命性的工业转型。在这一过程中，再次是自上而下的国家行动、而非自下而上的社会创议，成为动力。
而且，如同过去一样，国家强制现代化的动机是担心自己在欧洲列强中的生存。因为彼得创造、曾足以击败拿破仑的强大战争机器，在1854—1864年克里米亚战争之后已不再具有国际竞争力。事实上，对俄国军事地位下降的认识，是亚历山大二世大改革的主要推动力。到1890年代，当欧洲正在分裂为中心的三国同盟和纵向两端的三国协约时，快速工业发展比以往任何时候都更加紧迫。
en: The final challenge put to Russia by the rest of Europe was that of the industrial revolution. Textile manufacture had arrived by the 1840s and a railroad boom by the 1860s, but it was only through the exertions of Finance Minister Sergei Witte in the 1890s that it became possible to speak of a revolutionary industrial transformation of Russia. In this process, once again, it was state action from above, rather than social initiative from below, that was the motive force.

And again, as in the past, the state’s motivation for forced modernization was concern for its survival among the powers of Europe. For the once mighty war machine that Peter had created and that had sufficed to defeat Napoleon was no longer competitive internationally after the Crimean War of 1854-1864. Indeed, recognition of Russia’s declining military status was a major impetus to Alexander II’s Great Reforms. By the 1890s, as Europe was dividing into a Triple Alliance at its center and a Triple Entente at its longitudinal extremities, rapid industrial development was a greater imperative than ever before.
