zh: 再一次，现代化被压缩和缩短，其后果并不完全是预期的那样。维特的工业化片面地朝向重工业和最先进的设备，大型工厂设在大城市。轻工业和消费品生产因此受到忽视，农民通过税收被榨取，以资助整个事业，却没有从中得到任何切实好处。
en: Once again, modernization was compressed and telescoped, and its consequences were not entirely what had been intended. Witte’s industrialization was lopsidedly oriented towards heavy industry and the most modern equipment, and large factories were located in the biggest cities. Light industry and the production of consumer goods were accordingly slighted, and the peasantry was squeezed through taxation to finance the whole undertaking without benefitting from it in any tangible way.

zh: 这场速成现代化的结果是双重的、矛盾的。一方面，到1914年，按总产出来说，俄国已成为世界第五工业强国，排在美国、德国、英国和法国之后，但领先于奥匈帝国、意大利和日本。另一方面，按人均产量计算，她的排名是欧洲最低的，并不比许多亚洲国家高多少。因此，俄国可以被自己的许多知识分子有理由地视为一个特殊而独立的文化实体，一个“欧亚”文明；
而像列宁这样初露头角的革命者，则可以把俄国视为“半殖民地”，既是一个剥削人的欧洲强国，又是一个被西方更先进帝国主义国家剥削的国家。
en: The results of this crash modernization were twofold and contradictory. On the one hand, Russia by 1914 had become, in terms of total output, the fifth-ranking industrial power in the world, behind the United States, Germany, Britain, and France, but ahead of Austria-Hungary, Italy, and Japan. On the other hand, in terms of per capita production, her rank was the lowest in Europe and not much above that of many Asian nations. Thus Russia could plausibly be viewed by many of her own intellectuals as a special and separate cultural entity, a “Eurasian” civilization;
budding revolutionaries such as Lenin, meanwhile, could see her as “semicolonial,” both an exploiting European power and a country exploited by the more advanced imperialist countries of the West.

zh: 俄国世纪末地位的又一个失衡，可以在其脆弱的领主—农民社会秩序中找到；两个新因素的加入使这一秩序更加岌岌可危：第一是一个工业工人阶级。它虽然人数不多，却集中在少数大型战略城市中心，因此对既定秩序具有分散农民从未有过的潜在危险。第二个新因素是由各种商业、技术和专业中产阶级组成的集合体。他们与工人集中在同样的城市中心，构成人口中受教育程度最高、最“欧洲化”的部分。因此，社会主义和自由主义——此前都局限于知识分子飘渺的领域——如今各自都有了现代政治支持群体；这些群体完全配得上“市民社会”这一称谓；这个术语来自古典欧洲政治理论。
en: Yet another imbalance in Russia’s fin-de-siècle status could be found in her fragile lord-peasant social order, which had been made even more precarious by the addition of two new elements: The first was an industrial working class. Though small in number, it was concentrated in a few large and strategic urban centers, and was therefore potentially dangerous to the established order in a way that the dispersed peasantry had never been. The second new element was an aggregate of various commercial, technical, and professional middle classes. Concentrated in the same urban centers as the workers, they constituted the most literate and “European” part of the population. Thus socialism and liberalism, hitherto both confined to the airy sphere of the intelligentsia, now each had a modern political clientele fully meriting the name “civil society,” a term employed in classical European political theory.

zh: 在这种环境下，要求社会参与公共事务和宪政政府的压力变得不可抗拒。然而，专制制度按其本质是传统军事君主制的表现，它像普鲁士或奥地利的表亲一样，无意放弃自己的特权。事实上，因为亚历山大二世被暗杀使政府相信任何进一步改革都极其危险，它顽固地抵制一切变革。与此同时，由于在仍然专制的俄国，社会紧张程度远高于半宪政的普鲁士或奥地利，激进知识分子数十年来关于以彻底的普罗米修斯式革命通往真正民主的幻想，仍然非常活跃。
en: Under such circumstances, the pressures for social participation in public affairs and for constitutional government became irresistible. Yet the autocracy, by its very nature the expression of traditional military monarchy, had no more intention of surrendering its prerogatives than did its Prussian or Austrian cousins. Indeed, because the assassination of Alexander II convinced the government that any further reform would be downright dangerous, it stubbornly dug in its heels against all change. At the same time, because the level of social tension in still autocratic Russia was much higher than in half-constitutional Prussia or Austria, the radical intelligentsia’s decades-old fantasy of total, Promethean revolution as the path to true democracy remained very much alive.

zh: 事实上，随着马克思主义开始在知识分子中与民粹主义争夺首要地位，这一幻想获得了新的力量。这首先是因为到1881年，民粹主义的两种策略——群众农民起义和精英恐怖——都失败了。因此，曾是民粹主义者的格奥尔基·普列汉诺夫得出结论：农民实际上是一个落后的阶级，其知识分子代言人是危险的骗子。因为俄国并不是历史普遍逻辑的例外；她通往民主革命的道路必须遵循西方从封建主义到资本主义再到社会主义的进程。1880年代，普列汉诺夫使马克思主义在俄国扎根；1890年代，维特的工业化产生了一个“无产阶级”，似乎证明他是对的。因此，到1900年，一部分社会主义知识分子把效忠对象从农民转向工人，工人现在被视为即将到来的民主革命的新“普遍阶级”。于是，俄国激进主义终于赶上了欧洲社会意识形态的终极，拥抱了现代时代的制胜幻想——马克思主义。
en: Indeed, this fantasy gained renewed strength as Marxism began to compete with Populism for primacy among the intelligentsia. This occurred first because of the failure, by 1881, of Populism’s two tactics: mass peasant insurrection and elite terror. Accordingly, the onetime Populist Georgii Plekhanov drew the conclusion that the peasantry was, in fact, a retrograde class and that its intellectual spokesmen were dangerous deceivers. For Russia was not an exception to the universal logic of history; her way to democratic revolution therefore must follow the Western progression from feudalism to capitalism to socialism. In the 1880s Plekhanov acclimated Marxism in Russia, and in the 1890s Witte’s industrialization produced a “proletariat” that seemed to prove him right. Thus, by 1900, a part of the socialist intelligentsia shifted its allegiance from the peasants to the workers, who were now seen as constituting the new “universal class” of the coming democratic revolution. And so Russian radicalism at last drew abreast of the ultimate in European social ideology and embraced the winning fantasy of the modern age, Marxism.

zh: 但俄国革命运动的力量并非仅来自俄国社会过程的历史逻辑。它的进展同样来自人类事务中那个巨大偶然因素——战争——的催化冲击。俄国第一场现代军事失败——克里米亚战争——触发了大改革及其随之而来的革命副产品。甚至俄国1877—1878年对土耳其的“胜利”战争，也大大加剧了与“土地与自由”相关的革命危机。这一连败持续到1904—1905年的日俄战争，俄国遭受了帝国主义时代最屈辱的失败：败给一个非欧洲的“黄种”强国。这最后一场战争还把已经严重的内部危机激化为1905年革命。
en: But the Russian revolutionary movement did not owe its strength to the historical logic of Russia’s social processes alone. It progressed as much through the catalytic impact of that great contingency of human affairs—war. Russia’s first modern military defeat, in the Crimean War, triggered the Great Reforms and their ensuing revolutionary spinoff. Even Russia’s “victorious” war against Turkey in 1877-1878 greatly aggravated the revolutionary crisis associated with Land and Freedom. This losing streak continued with the Russo-Japanese War of 1904-1905, in which Russia suffered the most humiliating type of defeat for the imperialist era: defeat at the hands of a non-European “yellow” power. This last war also inflamed an already acute internal crisis to produce the Revolution of 1905.

zh: 这一事件虽然后来被1917年革命所掩盖，却常常被描绘成一场“工人革命”、红色十月的“彩排”。
然而事实上，1905年是一场彻底“正常的”欧洲革命，即马克思主义者会称之为“资产阶级”革命的那种。也就是说，它是一场针对旧制度的政治革命，主张宪政政府、立法议会和所有公民在法律面前平等。大多数参与者的目标中没有任何社会主义成分，产业工人只是参与其中的社会要素之一。实际上，这场革命由具有自由主义倾向的专业阶层和贵族领导，得到国内几乎所有城市要素的支持，其目标是自由民主的。

当然，工人在革命事件中发挥了重要的战术作用，因为他们有能力瘫痪经济和交通系统——也就是说，作为一支直接行动的力量，类似于1789—1793年自由革命中的巴黎平民无套裤汉。工人的作用在十月总罢工中尤为明显，那次罢工最终使专制制度屈服，迫使其授予一个立法杜马。但这场工人行动主义从未使运动具有阶级性质或独特的“无产阶级”政治目标。而社会主义政党——孟什维克和布尔什维克社会民主党人（SDs），以及新民粹主义的社会主义革命党人（SRs）——只发挥了次要的组织作用，远远落后于新兴的自由派立宪民主党人（Kadets）。
en: This event, although it came to be overshadowed by the Revolution of 1917, is all too often portrayed as a “workers’ revolution,” the “dress rehearsal” for Red October.

In fact, however, 1905 was a thoroughly “normal” European revolution, the kind that Marxists would characterize as “bourgeois.” That is, it was a political revolution against an Old Regime, in favor of constitutional government, a legislative parliament, and the equality of all citizens before the law. There was nothing socialist about the aims of most of its participants, and the industrial workers were only one of the social elements involved. In reality, the Revolution was led by the liberal professional classes and the gentry, it was supported by virtually all the urban elements in the country, and its aims were liberal-democratic.

The workers, of course, played a major tactical role in the revolutionary events because of their ability to paralyze the economy and the transportation system—that is, as a force for direct action analogous to that of the Parisian plebs, the

, in the liberal revolution of 1789-1793. The role of the workers was particularly evident in the October general strike, which at last brought the autocracy to its knees and compelled it to grant a legislative Duma. But at no time did this worker activism give the movement a class character or political aims that were distinctively “proletarian.” And the socialist parties—the Menshevik and Bolshevik Social Democrats, or SDs, and the neo-Populist Socialist Revolutionaries, or SRs—played only a minor organizational role, one far behind that of the emerging liberal Constitutional Democrats, or Kadets.

zh: 尽管如此，这场半截子革命最终是俄国自由主义的一次重大失败，这与1848年德意志革命是中欧自由主义的一次失败非常相似。因为在德国和俄国两种情况下，革命都被保守派赢得；保守派在整个激进风暴中设法保住了武装力量，从而镇压了“街头”。因此，两种情况的结局都是一种所谓的“假宪政主义”（
），即君主授予一个立法议会，但不接受政府向议会负责。在俄国，这种安排使杜马中的立宪民主党人对国家状况承担了一定责任，却没有获得任何相应的宪政权力。
en: Nonetheless, this demi-Revolution turned out to be a significant defeat for Russian liberalism, in very much the same way that the Revolution of 1848 in the Germanics was a defeat for Central European liberalism. For in both the German and the Russian cases the revolution was won by the conservatives, who, throughout the radical storm, managed to hold on to the armed forces and thus to put down the “street.” In both cases, therefore, the outcome was what was called a

, or a pseudoconstitutionalism, in which the monarchy granted a legislative parliament but did not accept that the government be responsible to it. In Russia, this arrangement gave the Kadets in the Duma a measure of responsibility for the state of the country without their gaining any corresponding constitutional power.

zh: 因此，自由派继续被专制制度所压制，而他们随之无力在关系大众的事务——首先是土地改革——上带来变化，损害了他们作为一支有效政治力量的地位。结果，当1912年后社会和政治鼓动恢复时，立宪民主党人处于不利地位，无法从中获益，左派的政治主动权因此转到了社会主义政党手中。俄国自由主义再一次在其左侧被革命社会主义淹没，这一模式可追溯到1861—1863年。因此，甚至在1917年革命开始之前，自由派实际上已经失去了领导政治的角色；通常被视为一场伟大革命最初温和阶段的东西，在俄国基本上已经结束。
en: Thus, the liberals continued to be overshadowed by the autocracy, and their concomitant inability to produce change in matters important to the mass of the population—above all, land reform-compromised them as an effective political force. In consequence, when social and political agitation resumed after 1912, the Kadets were poorly positioned to profit from it, and the political initiative on the Left therefore passed to the socialist parties. Once again Russian liberalism was overrun on its left by revolutionary socialism, in the pattern going back to 1861-1863. Thus, even before the Revolution of 1917 began, the liberals in effect had already lost their leading political role, and what is usually considered the initial, moderate phase of a great revolution was basically over in Russia.

zh: 正是这一政治、经济、社会和文化遗产，被俄国历史带入了1917年的革命爆炸以及由此产生的新苏维埃秩序。在评估俄国对苏维埃社会主义混合体的独特贡献之前，我们该如何概括旧制度政治文化的显著特征？
en: It is this political, economic, social, and cultural heritage that Russian history brought to the revolutionary explosion of 1917 and to the new Soviet order that emerged from it. As a preliminary to assessing the uniquely Russian contribution to the Soviet socialist mix, how may we characterize the salient traits of old-regime political culture?

zh: 这些特征中的第一个，无疑是俄国政府结构和社会结构的软弱与脆弱。一个粗陋的军事—官僚专制制度，凌驾于一个原始的两阶级领主—农民社会之上；国家的政治压迫，加上农奴制的社会压迫，造成了一种比任何其他欧洲国家都更大的系统性不稳定。结果，从十六世纪后期到十八世纪，俄国历史以一种独特的方式被巨大的农民起义所打断——动乱时期、斯捷潘·拉辛、布拉文、普加乔夫的起义——这些起义远远超过西方一切农民暴动，并危及社会秩序和国家本身的存在。甚至在十九世纪，当普希金所说的“没有头脑、没有怜悯”的俄国式暴动已不再发生时，群众无政府的幽灵仍然笼罩着这个制度。
en: The first of these traits is no doubt the weakness and fragility of Russian governmental and social structures. A crude military-bureaucratic autocracy capped a primitive two-class lord-peasant society, and the political oppressiveness of the state, in conjunction with the social oppressiveness of serfdom, created a systemic instability greater than in any other European nation. In consequence, Russian history from the late sixteenth through the eighteenth century was punctuated in a unique fashion by huge peasant revolts—those of the Time of Troubles, Stenka Razin, Bulavin, Pugachev—that far surpassed all Western jacqueries and called into question the very existence of the social order and the state. Even in the nineteenth century, when Pushkin’s “mindless and pitiless” Russian
had ceased to be practiced, the specter of mass anarchy still hung over the system.

zh: 正因如此，自由社会主义者亚历山大·赫尔岑才能宣称，俄国制度就像一个“临时营地”，很容易被革命风暴扫除。同样，革命社会主义者彼得·特卡乔夫（常被视为列宁的先驱）在1870年代论证说，俄国结构的脆弱性使得一场预防性的社会主义革命成为可能，而且可以在资本主义发展使国家社会制度多样化并固化之前进行。
用古典政治理论的语言来说，由于旧制度俄国的“市民社会”异常薄弱，国家便过度肥大，从而使整个制度独特地容易受到革命行动的打击。
en: It was for this reason that the liberal socialist Aleksandr Herzen could declare that the Russian system resembled a “temporary bivouac” that could easily be swept away by a revolutionary storm. Likewise, the revolutionary socialist Petr Tkachev (who has often been seen as a precursor of Lenin) could argue in the 1870s that the fragility of Russia’s structures made possible a preventive socialist revolution before the development of capitalism had diversified and solidified the country’s social system.

To put this insight in the language of classical political theory, because the “civil society” of old-regime Russia was exceptionally weak, the state had hypertrophied, thus making the whole system uniquely vulnerable to revolutionary action.

zh: 造成不稳定的俄国民族遗产的第二个方面，是十九世纪俄国知识分子的极端主义倾向。埃德蒙·伯克和托克维尔在著名檄文中对十八世纪法国不切实际、意识形态化的知识分子的一切严厉批评，都更适用于革命前的俄国知识分子。原因有二。第一，俄国知识分子出现时，领主和农民之间尚未形成西欧更常见的中间阶层。他们悬在半空，缺乏在社会中具有实际作用的社会群体作为根基，因此格外依赖纯粹理论，也从不必让理论接受现实政治的检验。这种极端主义的第二个原因，是俄国知识分子出现于欧洲文化发展的晚期，继承了英国、法国和德国思想传统的全部惊人包袱。而这些传统的深远含义远非一个以农奴制为基础的专制制度所能顺利容纳，结果便是一份过于丰盛的意识形态食粮和长期的智识消化不良。
en: A second aspect of the Russian national heritage that made for instability was the nineteenth-century Russian intelligentsia’s propensity for maximalism. All of the strictures that Edmund Burke and Tocqueville, in famous diatribes, levelled against the impractical and ideological intellectuals of eighteenth-century France apply even more strongly to the pre-Revolutionary Russian intelligentsia. This is so for two reasons. The first is that the Russian intelligentsia came into existence before the creation of the more usual intermediary classes between lords and peasants that were found farther West. Suspended in midair, without roots in social groupings with a practical role in society, to an exceptional degree the intelligentsia fell back on theory alone, and never had to confront it with the test of real politics. The second reason for this maximalism was that the Russian intelligentsia, appearing late in Europe’s cultural development, inherited the whole staggering baggage of the English, French, and German intellectual traditions. And because the far-reaching implications of these traditions were quite beyond the capacity of a serf-based autocracy to accommodate smoothly, the result was an overrich ideological diet and a chronic intellectual indigestion.

zh: 我们还可以加上俄国知识生活中倾向于道德主义的特性——这一品质使俄国十九世纪文学如此伟大，因而对较为厌倦的西方公众如此有吸引力。这种道德主义首先表现为毫不掩饰地关注人类处境的大问题；托尔斯泰——通过他的皮埃尔·别祖霍夫、普拉东·卡拉塔耶夫、列文，或通过他自己广为人知的个人探索——是这一模式无与伦比的艺术家。但这种道德主义很少是抽象和理论的，很少转向某种普遍绝对命令的超越性圣杯。它典型地表现为对社会和政治中伦理之具体应用的压倒性关切。
en: We may add to all this a Russian propensity for moralism in intellectual life—a quality that has made Russia’s nineteenth-century literature so great, and therefore so appealing to the more jaded Western public. This moralism expressed itself, first, in unabashed preoccupation with the Big Questions of the human condition, a mode of which Tolstoy—in the persons of his Pierre Bezukhov, Platon Karataev, Levin, or in his own well-publicized personal questing—is the unsurpassed artist. But this moralism was rarely abstract and theoretical. turned toward the transcendental Holy Grail of some universal Categorical Imperative. It was characteristically expressed in an overriding concern for the concrete application of ethics to society and politics.

zh: 因此，俄国政治思想被诸如“谁之罪？”“谁是人民之友？”“怎么办？”这样的道德和实践问题所支配。然而，这种倾向绝不是俄国灵魂某种特殊宗教品质的表现，不像尼古拉·别尔嘉耶夫及其西方模仿者要我们相信的那样。俄国公共生活中极端主义倾向的主要来源，毋宁说是：直到1905年，西欧所实践的真实政治在俄国是非法的，这意味着俄国的一切政治都自动地既是先验的，又是革命的。因此，我们再次面对一般现代文化模式的压缩、缩短和倒置，正是这些使落后的俄国成为共同欧洲主题上一个截然不同的变奏。
en: Thus Russian political thought was dominated by such moral and practical questions as, Who is to blame? Who are the friends of the people? What is to be done? This propensity, however, was by no means the expression of some special religious qualities of the Russian soul, as Nicholas Berdiaev and his Western emulators would have us believe. Rather, the major source of the tendency to maximalism in Russian public life was that, until 1905, real politics as practiced in Western Europe were illegal, and this meant that all politics in Russia were automatically both

and revolutionary. So once again we are confronted with the compressing, telescoping, and inverting of general modern modes of culture that make backward Russia a radically distinctive variation on common European themes.

zh: 结果是，俄国政党在1905年前夕出现时，全都属于一种不寻常的类型。在西方，政党只有在通过选举进行治理成为可能之后才被创造出来，其目的是赢得选票，然后合宪地行使权力。正如我们所见，政治正是这样第一次分为左派和右派。然而在俄国，“政党”在选举和宪政政府存在之前就出现了。因此，这些政党实际上是密谋团体，其目的与其说是合宪治理，不如说是推动革命。甚至法治主义的自由派——1905年后成为立宪民主党人（Kadets）——也不得不接受革命作为宪政的助产士。而所有位于立宪民主党人左侧的政党，都把对制宪会议的承诺从属于社会革命。维克多·切尔诺夫的新民粹主义社会主义革命党人（SRs）以农民的名义说话。“温和的”孟什维克社会民主党人尤利·马尔托夫以“成熟的”工人阶级名义说话，其模式是发达的欧洲国家。而更不耐烦的布尔什维克马克思主义者弗拉基米尔·乌里扬诺夫—列宁，在1905年后以工人和农民、或至少是农民较贫困阶层的名义说话。
en: In consequence, Russian political parties, when they emerged on the eve of 1905, were all of an unusual type. In the West, parties had been created only once it became possible to govern through elections, and their purpose was to win the vote and then exercise power constitutionally. This, as we have seen, was how politics first became divided into a Left and a Right. In Russia, however, “parties” emerged before elections and constitutional government existed. These parties, therefore, were in effect conspiracies designed more to promote revolution than to govern constitutionally. Even the legalistic liberals—after 1905 to become the Constitutional Democrats, or Kadets—had to accept revolution as the midwife of constitutionalism. And all the parties to the left of the Kadets subordinated their commitment to a constituent assembly to social revolution. The neo-Populist Socialist Revolutionaries, or SRs, of Victor Chernov spoke in the name of the peasantry. The “moderate” Menshevik Social Democrats of Iulii Martov spoke in the name of a “mature” working class, on the model of the developed European countries. And the more impatient Bolshevik Marxists of Vladimir Ulianov-Lenin, after 1905, spoke in the name of both the workers and the peasants, or at least of the peasantry’s poorer strata.

zh: 然而，这种政治活动在很大程度上只是“以……的名义”，因为所有俄国政党都由知识分子支配。在社会上，这些政党不仅以其假定的客户群体相区别，也以其知识领袖的素质和地位相区别。在立宪民主党人中，我们看到高水平的创造才能、世界主义文化和坚实的学术或社会地位，如帕维尔·米留可夫教授或经济学家彼得·司徒卢威。随着我们向左移动，政治知识分子变得更加外省、社会地位更加边缘、文化上更加纯粹的俄国化、纲领上更加意识形态化。因此，社会主义革命党的活动分子主要扎根于地方自治局的教师和技术专家之中。孟什维克大量吸收城市小知识分子，尤其是犹太人（他们在帝俄中按定义就是边缘化的）以及边缘民族格鲁吉亚人。最后，布尔什维克活动分子则招募自一个更加异质、更加外省、主要是大俄罗斯人的小知识分子群体；他们的正规教育水平最低，因为他们的激进主义常常使他们辍学或被学术体系开除——列宁和斯大林就是两个例子。
en: Yet this political activity was very much only “in the name of,” for all Russian parties were dominated by intelligentsia. Socially, these parties differed in terms not just of their presumed clientele, but also of the quality and status of their intellectual leaders. Among the Kadets we find a high level of creative talent, cosmopolitan culture, and solid academic or social standing in such figures as Professor Pavel Miliukov or the economist Petr Struve. As we move to the left, the political intellectuals become more provincial, more marginal in social position, more purely Russian in culture, and more ideological in their programs. Thus the SR activists had their principal roots among the schoolteachers and technical specialists of the

. The Mensheviks drew heavily on the urban petty intelligentsia, particularly among Jews (who were by definition marginalized in Imperial Russia), and in the marginal nation of Georgia. Finally, the Bolshevik activists were recruited from a more heterogeneous, provincial, and largely Great Russian petty intelligentsia; and they had the lowest level of formal education because their radicalism all too frequently led them to drop out of, or be expelled from, the academic system—Lenin and Stalin being two cases in point.

zh: 然而，社会地位的边缘性将被证明并不妨碍在第一次世界大战的熔炉中成就伟大命运——铁匠之子墨索里尼和海关官员之子希特勒就是两个例子。既然我们知道列宁及其杂七杂八的追随者将在俄国获胜，最好在这里、在旧制度和他们默默无闻的时期讨论他和他的布尔什维克，而不是在后面、在他们革命胜利的背景中讨论。
en: Yet marginal social status would prove to be no bar to great destinies in the crucible of the First World War—the blacksmith’s son, Mussolini, and the custom official’s son, Hitler, are two examples. And since we know that Lenin and his motley followers are going to win in Russia, it is best to discuss him and his Bolsheviks here, in the context of the Old Regime and the period of their obscurity, rather than later, in the context of their revolutionary triumph.

zh: 列宁与布尔什维主义
en: LENIN AND BOLSHEVISM

zh: 列宁是俄罗斯帝国秩序中最优秀部分的产物：教育体系和道德主义知识分子的文化。他生于1870年，出身于伏尔加河畔辛比尔斯克城一个小康贵族和中层国家官员的家庭，他的父亲在那里升至学校督学。
en: Lenin was the product of what was best in the Russian Imperial order: the educational system and the culture of the moralistic intelligentsia. Born in 1870, he was from a background of modest gentry and middling state officialdom in the Volga city of Simbirsk, where his father had risen to become inspector of schools.

zh: 列宁沿着自1860年代以来通往这一职业的通常道路成为革命者：青年理想与国家权力之间的冲突导致惩罚和对制度的离心。这一过程始于他的哥哥亚历山大加入民意党的继承组织，并于1887年被处决。家庭被上流社会排斥，列宁很快被喀山大学开除。虽然他最终通过函授课程成为律师（一个他从未从事的职业），但他与制度彻底疏离。直到二十三岁都生活在伏尔加河畔的外省城市，他从哥哥那种车尔尼雪夫斯基传统的民粹主义，转向了普列汉诺夫的新马克思主义。
en: Lenin became a revolutionary by the usual path to that vocation since the 1860s: conflict between youthful idealism and state power leading to punishment and disaffection from the system. The process began when his older brother Alexander joined a successor to the Will of the People and was executed in 1887. The family was ostracized by established society and Lenin was soon expelled from the University of Kazan. Though he eventually became a lawyer (a profession he never practiced) by taking correspondence courses, he was totally alienated from the system. Living in provincial Volga cities until the age of twenty-three, he evolved from his older brother’s Populism in the tradition of Chernyshevskii to the new Marxism of Plekhanov.

children: 〔译注〕原书称列宁从未从事律师工作；另有记载称他1892—1893年曾在萨马拉短期执业。
〔译注〕原书称列宁从未从事律师工作；另有记载称他1892—1893年曾在萨马拉短期执业。

zh: 九十年代中期，列宁搬到圣彼得堡，在俄国第一次大规模工业罢工期间开始在工人中鼓动，从而成为一名职业革命者。按照这一新职业的经典公式，接着是逮捕，然后流放西伯利亚——伴随着大量研究和出版——最后在1900年逃往国外，在那里一直待到1917年4月（除了1905年的短暂返回）。在流亡中，列宁一心一意地致力于建立一个最终夺取政权的党。这并不是说他就不是一个深度投入的马克思主义者和理论家，因为他两者都是，总是费尽心力把自己的纲领建立在马克思主义原则之上。但首先，他是一个革命的实践者和权力的技术员。因此，他的伟大任务是把马克思主义的总体世界观改造得适应俄国局势的特殊性。
en: In the mid-nineties Lenin moved to St. Petersburg, began agitating among the workers during Russia’s first major industrial strikes, and so became a professional revolutionary. In the classic formula of this new calling, arrest followed and then exile to Siberia—accompanied by much research and publication—and finally, in 1900, escape abroad, where he would remain (except for a brief return in 1905) until April 1917. In emigration Lenin was single-mindedly devoted to building a party for the eventual seizure of power. This is not to say that he was not also a deeply committed Marxist and a theoretician, for he was both, always taking immense pains to ground his programs in Marxist principles. But above all he was a practitioner of revolution and a technician of power. Thus his great task was to adapt the general worldview of Marxism to the particularities of the Russian situation.

zh: 后来，1917年之后，社会民主党人声称列宁的党不是真正的马克思主义，而是向民意党密谋传统的倒退，因而是对俄国政治斗争压迫条件的回应。然而，所有俄国政党都面临同样的条件，却只有布尔什维克成为一个密谋组织。与社会主义革命党人的对比澄清了其原因。社会主义革命党的恐怖翼“战斗组织”是密谋性的，但主要政党尽管成员众多，结构却如此松散，以致它是三个社会主义团体中政治上最无效的。这不仅因为它的选民是分散的农民；更因为社会主义革命党人缺乏结构化的意识形态。简言之，他们的意识形态是：权力归人民，土地归农民，“现在就革命”——这些泛泛之谈几乎没有操作重点。
en: Later, after 1917, Social Democrats alleged that the Leninist Party was not authentically Marxist, but a throwback to the conspiratorial tradition of the Will of the People and, as such, a response to the oppressive conditions of political struggle in Russia. However, all Russian parties faced the same conditions, yet only the Bolsheviks became a conspiratorial organization. The reasons for this are clarified by the contrast with the SRs. The SRs’ terrorist wing, the Combat Organization, was conspiratorial, but the main party, despite its large membership, was so loosely structured that it was the least effective politically of the three socialist groups. This was not just because its constituency was the dispersed peasantry; it was even more because the SRs lacked a structured ideology. Simply put, their ideology was: Power to the people, land to the peasants, and “revolution now”—generalities that had little operational focus.

zh: 另一方面，社会民主党人获得优越组织能力，不仅来自他们集中的工人“基础”，也来自其意识形态的理性主义结构。然而，这种意识形态，正如我们所见，是一个雅努斯双面的东西。因此，在一个共同的世界观内部，孟什维克强调其正式信条和历史逻辑是革命的关键，而布尔什维克则把这一角色赋予“科学的革命意识”。而当只有一种真学说时，人们便强烈倾向于相信只能有一个拥有单一“正确”路线的真党。
en: The SDs, on the other hand, derived their superior capacity for organization not only from their concentrated worker “base,” but also from the rationalistic structure of their ideology. Yet this ideology, as we have seen, was a Janus-headed affair. Thus, within a shared world-view, the Mensheviks emphasized its formal tenets and the logic of history as the key to revolution, whereas the Bolsheviks assigned that role to “scientific revolutionary consciousness.” And when there is only one true doctrine, the tendency is strong to believe there can be only one true party with a single “correct” line.

zh: 因此，列宁与马克思相遇的结果，是创造了现代最非凡的政治组织：共产党。马克思的《宣言》已经赋予他称为“共产党人”的人一种先锋角色，而且他确实以一种可公正地称为原型列宁主义的专制和操纵方式管理第一国际。但1848年后欧洲相对稳定的条件不利于这类做法的制度化；因此，西欧马克思主义与群众性社会民主党联系在一起，后者越来越关心赢得选举，而不是制造革命。到1900年，只有俄国条件仍然使马克思主义的“先锋主义”潜力得以发挥出来。
en: The result of Lenin’s encounter with Marx, therefore, was the creation of the most extraordinary political institution of the modern age: the Communist Party. Marx’s

already accorded a vanguard role to people he called “the Communists” and he certainly ran the First International in an authoritarian and manipulative manner that can fairly be called proto-Leninist. But the relatively stable conditions of post-1848 Europe did not lend themselves to the institutionalization of such practices; so Western European Marxism became identified with mass Social Democratic parties that increasingly were concerned with winning elections rather than with making a revolution. By 1900, only Russian conditions still made it possible to bring out the “vanguardist” potential of Marxism.

zh: 1901年，俄国马克思主义开始围绕流亡报纸《火星报》（

），在年长的普列汉诺夫和较年轻的列宁、尤利·马尔托夫领导下组织起来。这家理论机关报试图协调俄国境内分散的马克思主义小组，以产生一个全国性的社会民主党。火星派的第一场战斗是说服知识分子：民粹主义关于农民革命将使俄国跳过资产阶级发展阶段的信念是一种幻想。相反，他们论证说，俄国像所有其他国家一样，必须走完通过资本主义的全程苦路，才能到达社会主义。因此，俄国革命将分为两个阶段，完全忠实于马克思主义的正式信条：即将到来的第一阶段将是资产阶级民主革命，而社会主义只有在第二阶段、一旦资本主义创造了必要的客观条件之后才会到来。
en: In 1901 Russian Marxism began to organize around the émigré newspaper

(The Spark) under the leadership of the elder Plekhanov and the younger Lenin and Iulii Martov. This theoretical organ sought to coordinate the scattered Marxist groups within Russia to produce a national Social Democratic Party. The Iskrists’ first battle was to convince the intelligentsia that the Populist belief in a peasant revolution that would permit Russia to skip over the bourgeois phase of development was an illusion. Instead, they argued, Russia, like all other countries, must suffer the full Way of the Cross through capitalism before reaching socialism. The Russian revolution, therefore, would be in two stages, in perfect fidelity to Marxism’s formal tenets: The impending first stage would be bourgeois democratic, while socialism would come only in a second stage, once capitalism had created the requisite objective conditions.

zh: 但火星派也面对马克思主义内部的敌人，即西方所谓的“修正主义”和俄国所谓的“经济主义”，两者都把马克思主义的革命目标从属于争取工人眼前物质改善的斗争。这种向改革主义的倒退，促使列宁对马克思主义学说作出了他最具决定性的贡献：先锋队政党理论，于1902年在一本以车尔尼雪夫斯基革命祈祷书命名的小册子《怎么办？》中提出。
这一理论宣称，工人单纯的“自发性”只能导致“工联主义”，因此必须从外部向无产阶级灌输“科学”革命理论的“意识”，而这种意识只能来自“资产阶级知识分子”中“受过教育”的成员。于是，列宁提出了他的“新型政党”观念，一个旨在“颠覆整个俄国”的党；其决定性特征在于，它将不是一个群众组织，而是一个由职业革命者组成的密谋团体。
en: But the Iskrists also faced an enemy within Marxism itself, one known as “revisionism” in the West and “economism” in Russia, both of which subordinated the revolutionary goal of Marxism to the struggle for the immediate material betterment of the workers. This backsliding into reformism provoked Lenin into his most decisive contribution to Marxist doctrine: the theory of the vanguard party, set forth in 1902 in a pamphlet called, after the title of Chernyshevskii’s revolutionary breviary,

This theory proclaimed that the mere “spontaneity” of the workers could lead only to “trade unionism” and that the proletariat, therefore, must be informed from without by the “consciousness” of “scientific” revolutionary theory, which could only come from “educated” members of the “bourgeois intelligentsia.” Thus Lenin launched the idea of his “party of a new type,” a party designed to “overturn all Russia” its defining characteristic was that it would not be a mass organization but a conspiratorial body of professional revolutionaries.

zh: 正是围绕这个组织问题，社会民主党人在1903年伦敦第一次代表大会上分裂：列宁坚持集中制，而马尔托夫和普列汉诺夫想要一个基础更广泛的运动。于是出现了两个俄国马克思主义派别：列宁的布尔什维克（多数派）和孟什维克（少数派），这两个名称来自会议最后投票中前者暂时占优。
en: It was precisely over this organizational issue that the SDs split at their first congress in London in 1903, with Lenin insisting on centralization but Martov and Plekhanov wanting a more broadly based movement. Thus there emerged two Russian Marxist factions: Lenin’s Bolsheviks, or majoritarians, and the Mensheviks, or minoritarians, so named because in the final votes of the meeting the former had a temporary edge.

children: 〔译注〕原书称1903年大会为第一次；该党第二次代表大会1903年先在布鲁塞尔举行，后转至伦敦。
〔译注〕原书称1903年大会为第一次；该党第二次代表大会1903年先在布鲁塞尔举行，后转至伦敦。

zh: 然而，就当时而言，两派在形式上仍统一在一个党内，其结构借自声望卓著的德国社会民主党。这些结构很容易为列宁的事业所用，因为它们已经提供了一种相当新型的政党组织。十九世纪的大多数政党都是小型精英团体：辉格党与托利党、自由党与保守党、奥尔良派与正统派、民主党与共和党——都缺乏结构化的组织。有组织的政党是十九世纪后期社会主义者的发明，而在这方面最早熟的是德国社会民主党。正是他们引入了党证、定期党费、党小组，以及从各级委员会到定期代表大会和常设中央委员会的等级制。他们这样做，部分是因为他们是一个受围攻的对手党——实际上是德意志帝国内部一个与主流社会对抗的次社会——部分是因为普选使这样一个群众党成为可能。
en: For the time being, however, the two factions remained formally united in a single party whose structures were borrowed from the prestigious Social Democracy of Germany. And these structures lent themselves readily to Lenin’s enterprise, for they already offered a quite new type of party organization. Most nineteenth-century parties were small and elitist affairs: Whigs and Tories, Liberals and Conservatives, Orleanists and Legitimists, Democrats and Republicans—all lacked structured organizations. Organized parties were a late-nineteenth-century invention of the socialists, and the most precocious in this matter were the German SDs. It was they who introduced party cards, regular dues, party cells, and a hierarchy of committees leading up to periodic congresses and a standing Central Committee. They did this in part because they were an embattled, adversary party—indeed a counter-society in Imperial Germany—and in part because universal suffrage made such a mass party possible.

zh: 但正如韦伯的学生罗伯特·米歇尔斯早在1911年在其关于社会民主党的经典研究《政党》中所指出的，社会民主党的组织模式不可避免地倾向于官僚制和寡头制，从而挫败平等主义（也抑制革命热情）。

不过，在德国的情况下，真正的选举使官僚寡头或多或少对基层负责。但如果在这样的结构中选举萎缩，权力金字塔就会倒转，党就会变成一种婉称为“民主集中制”的独裁，其主动性自上而下流动。这是罗莎·卢森堡在现在讨论的时期对列宁纲领的批评。当然，这正是他的党掌权后所发生的事。还可以补充说，第一次世界大战后，革命右翼的政党模仿其社会民主党和共产党对手，也采用了类似的官僚集中制，而共产党人把同一种组织传给了中国的国民党。
en: But as Weber’s pupil, Robert Michels, pointed out as early as 1911 in his classic study of the SDs,
, the Social Democratic mode of organization inevitably tends to bureaucracy and oligarchy, thus thwarting egalitarianism (and also braking revolutionary élan).

Still, in the German case, genuine elections made the bureaucratic oligarchy more or less responsive to the base, But if ever elections atrophied in such a structure, the pyramid of power would be inverted and the party would become a dictatorship under the euphemistic designation “democratic centralism,” where initiative flowed from the top down. This was Rosa Luxemburg’s criticism of Lenin’s program during the period now under discussion. And this, of course, is precisely what happened once his party came to power. To this it may be added that a similar bureaucratic centralism was adopted by parties of the revolutionary Right after the First World War in imitation of their SD and Communist adversaries, and the Communists transmitted the same type of organization to China’s Kuomintang.

zh: 因此，每个社会民主党内部都潜伏着一个列宁式的党。稍微前瞻一点，这一情况在很大程度上解释了左派这些“敌对兄弟”的爱恨关系，以及人民阵线反复出现的幻景。但反命题是否成立，即每个列宁式政党内部都有一个挣扎着重生的社会民主党？许多改革派共产党人和西方修正主义历史学家认为是这样。但这个问题的答案必须等待对实际记录的考察。目前只需指出，共产主义内部存在一部蛰伏的社会民主党“宪法”，这将在苏联事务中发挥真实作用。
en: Thus, in every SD Party there is a Leninist Party
. To anticipate a bit, this circumstance goes far to explain the love-hate relationship of these

of the Left and the recurrent mirage of the Popular Front as well, But is the reverse of this proposition true, namely, that in every Leninist Party there is a social democracy struggling to be reborn? Numerous reform Communists and Western revisionist historians have thought so. But the answer to this question must await examination of the actual record. For the moment, suffice it to note that the existence of a dormant SD “constitution” within Communism would play a real role in Soviet affairs.

zh: 因此，布尔什维主义显现出来的第一个决定性特征不是社会性的，而是组织性的；布尔什维克的实质性纲领将始终从属于这一政治要求。

而这些纲领很快出现，通常是通过反对孟什维克。第一，到1905年，列宁从民粹派那里学了一半，主张工农联盟，以进行资产阶级本身过于怯懦而无法完成的反对专制的“资产阶级”革命；而孟什维克则主张支持立宪民主党人实现政治民主，然后等待一段未指明的时期，让社会主义革命的条件成熟。第二，1912年，列宁采纳了另一个是否符合马克思主义颇可怀疑的观念，支持帝国少数民族的自决权，以制造进一步的革命压力。第三，同样在1912年，列宁把自己的派别建立为一个独立组织，声称是俄国唯一真正的马克思主义政党，实际上把孟什维克作为偏离分子清洗出去——这一先例在1920年代布尔什维主义内部的派系斗争和1930年代的清党中不会被忘记。
en: Thus the first defining characteristic of Bolshevism to emerge was not social but organizational; Bolshevik substantive programs would always be subordinated to this political imperative.

And these programs quickly emerged, usually through opposition to the Mensheviks. First, by 1905 Lenin, taking half a leaf from the Populists, was advocating an alliance of workers and peasants to make the “bourgeois” revolution against autocracy that the bourgeoisie itself was too cowardly to carry out, while the Mensheviks favored supporting the Kadets to achieve political democracy and then waiting an unspecified period for conditions to mature for a socialist revolution. Second, in 1912 Lenin adopted another dubiously Marxist idea by espousing self-determination for the Empire’s minority nationalities in order to generate further revolutionary pressure. Third, again in 1912, Lenin set up his faction as a separate organization claiming to be the one true Marxist party in Russia, in effect purging the Mensheviks as deviationists—a precedent that would not be forgotten in the factional fights within Bolshevism in the 1920s and the Party Purges of the 1930s.

zh: 最后，战争爆发后，列宁在《帝国主义是资本主义的最高阶段》中作出了他对马克思主义的主要理论贡献。对马克思来说，资本主义致命的内部矛盾本应在欧洲工业社会中展开；列宁把这些矛盾全球化，变成先进欧洲垄断性“金融资本”与其落后“殖民地和半殖民地”依附地之间的对立，后者由此成为一种行星性的无产阶级或普遍阶级。在这一愿景中，欧洲列强为补偿国内利润下降而瓜分亚洲和非洲的世纪末争夺，只能以敌对帝国主义阵营之间的世界大战告终；而从这场末日灾难中最终将产生世界社会主义革命。此外，由于俄国同时具有剥削国和半殖民地国家的双重不稳定，这场革命有可能在沙皇帝国开始。因此，“资本主义链条中最薄弱的一环”在逻辑上将成为世界革命的最强力量。
en: Finally, after the outbreak of war, Lenin made his major theoretical contribution to Marxism in

children: Imperialism, the Highest Stage of Capitalism

en: . For Marx, the fatal internal contradictions of capitalism were to have worked themselves out in the industrial societies of Europe; Lenin globalized these contradictions into an antithesis between the monopolistic “finance capital” of advanced Europe and its backward “colonial and semicolonial” dependencies, which thereby became a kind of planetary proletariat or universal class. In this vision, the

scramble of the European powers to divide up Asia and Africa in order to compensate for falling profits at home could only end in world war between rival imperialist camps; and out of this apocalypse would at last come the world socialist revolution. Moreover, since Russia suffered the double instability of being both an exploiting and a semicolonial country, this revolution might conceivably begin in the Tsarist Empire. The “weakest link of the capitalist chain” would thus logically become the strongest force for world revolution.

zh: 简言之，从1902年起，列宁在其演进的每一个阶段都以一种逐步违背马克思主义正式信条的方式解释马克思主义，并改写其官方历史逻辑，以适应俄国的落后。然而，在这样做时，他始终忠于马克思主义的深层结构，这一结构把社会剥夺和非人化置于阶级斗争的造物主地位。因为沙皇帝国的工人和农民、甚至各民族，事实上是欧洲最受剥夺、最被非人化的大众，几乎真的像《宣言》结尾所说，“除了锁链没有什么可失去的”。这些对马克思主义的调整，产生了一种隐含的战略：“现在就革命”，首先在俄国革命；并且只有在列宁自己的党领导下革命。然而，他推进这一大胆纲领时没有一丝个人野心。像马克思一样，他简单而毫不怀疑地确信，凭借自己的“科学意识”，他永远正确，因此他所有的社会主义对手事实上都是“小资产阶级”叛徒。
en: In short, at each stage of his evolution from 1902 onward, Lenin construed Marxism in a manner that progressively contravened its formal tenets and recast its official logic of history to accommodate Russian backwardness. Yet in so doing, he always remained faithful to Marxism’s deeper structure, which privileged social deprivation and dehumanization as the demiurge of the class struggle. For the workers and peasants, and even the nationalities, of the tsarist Empire were in fact the most deprived and dehumanized masses in Europe, with almost literally “nothing to lose but their chains,” as the finale of the

has it. The result of these adaptations of Marxism was an implied strategy of “revolution now” of revolution first of all in Russia; and of revolution only under the leadership of Lenin’s own party. Yet he advanced this bold program without a trace of personal ambition. Like Marx, he was simply and unquestioningly convinced that in his “scientific consciousness” he was always right, and that all his socialist rivals therefore were in fact “petty bourgeois” traitors.

zh: 然而，到1914年，列宁所代表的那种追求彻底目标的激进主义似乎并不是俄国权力的主要竞争者。当然，俄国政治生活强烈偏向左派，但这个左派是多样化的，其重心大约在立宪民主党人和社会主义革命党人之间。列宁和他的运动对大多数人口来说基本上不为人知。此外，1905年革命的相对失败使许多知识分子醒悟，放弃其长期信奉的进步、唯物论和人民革命的教条；这一变化在1909年出版的一本名为《路标》（
）的知识分子自我批评文集中表现得淋漓尽致。而同一时期俄国文学白银时代的审美文化，更是在知识分子内部培育了多元主义。
en: As of 1914, however, the kind of maximalist radicalism represented by Lenin did not seem to be a prime contender for power in Russia. Certainly, Russian political life was strongly weighted to the Left, but this Left was a variegated one, with its center of gravity somewhere between the Kadets and the SRs. Lenin and his movement were largely unknown to most of the population. Moreover, the relative failure of the Revolution of 1905 had disabused much of the intelligentsia of its long-time dogmas of progress, materialism, and popular revolution, a change made manifest in a spectacular volume of intelligentsia self-criticism called
(Signposts), published in 1909. And the aesthetic culture of the Silver Age of Russian literature during these same years fostered pluralism within the intelligentsia even more.

zh: 最后，在社会“基础”层面，世纪初的转变意味着俄国与更先进西方国家之间的结构性差距在不断缩小。因此，对大多数俄国知识分子——无论自由派、社会主义者还是不问政治者——来说，俄国的未来显然在于完全的“欧洲化”。在这种观点中，那些使她一只脚仍留在亚洲专制主义中的传统因素，被视为过去的残余，而非未来的先兆。
en: At the “base” of society, finally, the transformations of the beginning of the century meant that the structural gap between Russia and the more advanced Western nations was constantly closing. Thus, to most of the Russian intelligentsia, whether liberal, socialist, or apolitical, Russia’s future clearly lay in her complete “Europeanization.” In this view, those elements of her heritage that left her with one foot in Asiatic despotism were deemed to be holdovers from the past rather than harbingers of the future.

zh: 这些残余的民族特性也不会凭简单的直接延续——更不用说直接的因果关系——成为未来的催化剂。俄国市民社会的薄弱和知识分子的极端主义，只有在通过泛欧洲的社会主义乌托邦折射之后，才能相互作用产生苏维埃主义。而通往这一所谓历史顶点的道路，只有通过第一次世界大战这场泛欧洲的大灾难，才能在俄国开辟。
en: Nor would these holdover national traits be the catalysts of the future in any simple sense of direct continuity, still less of causality. The weakness of Russian civil society and the maximalism of the intelligentsia could react with one another to produce Sovietism only when refracted through the pan-European utopia of socialism. And the path to this would-be culmination of history could be blazed in Russia only by the pan-European cataclysm of the First World War.

zh: 其结果将是俄国与西方关系的一次惊人变化：在对民粹主义幻想的马克思主义置换中，欧洲最落后的国家突然至少在抱负上成为最先进的国家；昔日的追随者成为领导者；各民族中的最后一个成为第一个。因为俄国从欧洲文化梯度的低端起跑，似乎能够从整个欧洲先前的发展中得出实践结论，从而压倒其他所有人的王牌。
en: The result would be an astounding change in Russia’s relationship to the West: In a Marxist transposition of the Populist fantasy, the most backward country of Europe suddenly became, at least in aspiration, the most advanced; the erstwhile follower became the leader; and the last among the peoples became the first. For Russia, starting from the low end of the European cultural gradient, appeared able to draw the practical conclusions from all of Europe’s anterior development, and so to trump everyone else’s ace.

了其他国家[即英国和法国]

对此可以补充两点：第一，德国人思考的东西远多于英国人和法国人实际做过的；第二，俄国人随后实际做了德国人仅仅想到的事情。因此，到1914年，俄国已准备成为整个现代世界的实践革命意识。

what other nations [i.e., England and France] have

To this it might be added, first, that the Germans had thought quite a bit more than the English and French had ever done; and second, that the Russians then actually did what the Germans had only thought of. And so, by 1914 Russia was poised to become the practical revolutionary consciousness of the entire modern world.
